questions.reviewCue: These are the roads between the stops, not the stops themselves.

questions.stem: Which of the four entities of a data flow diagram transforms incoming data into outgoing data?

answers.rationale: This entity transforms incoming data flows into outgoing data flows.
Data stores are repositories for data that is not moving.
Data flows are the movement of data, not the step that changes it.

questions.reviewCue: Like a kitchen that takes in raw ingredients and sends out finished meals, this symbol changes what passes through it.

questions.stem: Which data flow diagram entity represents sources or destinations outside the specified system boundary?

answers.rationale: Data flows are the movement of data in the system, not its sources or destinations.
Processes transform incoming data flows into outgoing data flows inside the system.
Data stores are repositories for data that is not moving.
This entity represents sources or destinations outside the specified system boundary.

questions.reviewCue: Think of the offices beyond the fence line that send data in or receive it while living apart from the system.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush picks a frame method for a switch on links where damaged frames are common. Each frame must sit in internal memory before it leaves, and a frame with an error in its last bytes must be dropped at the switch. The switch must be characterized by the one forwarding method it supports. Which method fits?

answers.rationale: This method sends bad frames on to the destination, so a damaged frame would leave the switch.
This method checks only the first 64 bytes, so an error in the last bytes would pass.
Holding each whole frame and dropping any with an error anywhere, as the one method a switch supports, matches every stated need.
This selects among methods to suit conditions, but this switch is characterized by the one method it supports.

questions.stem: On core links, where errors are few and speed is important, an airman sets one method on a switch for all traffic at all times. Each frame starts out of the outgoing interface before the switch has received the whole of it. Hosts sometimes receive frames with damage in their first bytes and ask their sources to resend them. Which method did he set?

keywords.text: ask their sources to resend them

answers.rationale: Sending each frame early and letting damaged frames reach hosts, which request a resend, fits all three facts.
This method holds the entire frame before sending, but here frames leave before they fully arrive.
This method checks the first 64 bytes, so damage there would be caught at the switch.
This picks a method by traffic conditions, but one method is set for all traffic at all times.

questions.stem: Traffic on an airman's segment changes through the day, but she sets one fixed method on the switch. The switch keeps only the first part of each frame, where breaks are most likely, and checks it before sending. The rest of each frame is still arriving when the switch starts sending it. Which method fits?

answers.rationale: This method leaves error checks to the destination, but this switch checks the first part before sending.
This method waits for the entire frame, but here sending starts while the rest still arrives.
This picks the method from traffic conditions, but this airman set one fixed method.
Checking only the early part of each frame, then sending before the rest arrives, with one fixed method, fits all facts.

questions.stem: An airman adds redundant links between switches so the building stays connected if one switch fails. She knows these extra paths alone can create a switch loop. She wants the switches to communicate with each other and keep the network safe from that loop. Which choice does this?

answers.rationale: This acts when traffic on a cable flows one way after a fault, but here the extra paths alone create the loop.
Switches communicating with each other to keep redundant paths from forming a loop is this loop-prevention protocol.
This puts a single port into a loop inconsistent state; it does not have the switches communicate with each other.
This advertises configurations to neighbors, but it does not keep the network safe from a loop.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush powers on a new switch whose table is empty and plugs in two computers on one cable each. The first computer sends a single frame to the second. The switch sends that frame out every port except the one it arrived on, and a moment later its table holds one entry. Which switch function is he watching?

answers.rationale: This function sends a frame out only its listed destination's interface, but this frame went out every other port.
Flooding a frame for an unlisted destination while the empty table gains its first entry is this function.
This function deals with extra paths, but each computer here has a single cable, so there is one path.
A storm needs devices rebroadcasting data endlessly in reply, but only one frame was sent here.

questions.stem: To remove a single point of failure, an airman adds a second cable between his two switches. Soon one frame is retransmitted endlessly, and the Media Access Control (MAC) address table becomes unstable. Which basic switch function must now handle the new setup?

answers.rationale: A second cable creates more than one path, and endless retransmission is what this basic function must handle.
This function fills the table, but the new trouble began with the second cable creating a second path.
This function sends frames out one interface; it does not handle a frame that is retransmitted endlessly.
Endless retransmission can grow into a storm, but a storm is a problem, and the question asks for a basic switch function.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush finds one redundant cable forming the only extra path between two switches. Hosts keep sending messages meant for every device, other devices send them back onto the link in reply, and soon all traffic stops. Each switch's table still shows every host on its usual port. Which problem has he found?

keywords.text: send them back onto the link

answers.rationale: Loops inside other loops need several extra paths, but only one extra path exists here.
Messages for every device being sent back onto the link until all traffic stops is this loop problem.
This problem makes the table keep changing where a device sits, but each table here still shows the usual ports.
A late collision is a transmission after another host's first 64 bytes; here devices are resending messages in reply.

questions.stem: An airman joins two switches with a second cable as a backup, giving one extra path. A server then gets two of the same message at the same moment, one from each segment, and the switch keeps rewriting which port it lists for that server. Traffic between other hosts still flows normally. Which problem is this?

answers.rationale: A storm overwhelms the whole network, but traffic between other hosts here still flows normally.
Loops inside other loops need several extra paths, but this second cable gives one extra path.
The same message arriving from two segments at once, so the table keeps changing the server's port, is this problem.
Recording senders is a normal switch function, while the question asks which problem is happening.

questions.stem: An airman replaces an old device that shared bandwidth among all its ports with a new one. The new device reads each frame's destination hardware address and sends it only out the intended device's port. It reads only Data-Link information, so broadcasts from any computer still reach every port. Which device did she install?

keywords.text: shared bandwidth among all its ports

answers.rationale: A hub repeats every frame out all other ports, but this device sends each frame to one intended port.
A router is a Layer 3 device whose interfaces are separate broadcast domains, yet here broadcasts reach every port.
A Layer 3 device adds routing, but this one reads only Data-Link information.
A Layer 2 device that sends frames only to their intended port while broadcasts still reach every port fits all facts.

questions.stem: An airman must change the settings on a new switch. She plugs a laptop running PuTTY straight into the switch with a cable. Through that cable she then types commands that the switch carries out. Which connection does she use?

answers.rationale: Direct local access from a laptop running terminal emulation software over a cable, to type configuration commands, is this connection.
End devices plug in here, but a laptop running terminal emulation software for direct local access uses another port.
This is used for remote management over a network interface, but her laptop is cabled straight into the switch.
A link between two network devices carries data between them, but her cable carries the commands she types to the switch.

questions.stem: An airman traces how a switch starts up. One component keeps what it holds saved while the switch is powered off, and each time the switch boots up, those contents are loaded for use. They are the software that the switch uses for all of its operations. Which component is it?

answers.rationale: This holds the diagnostic and boot up routines, not the software loaded for the switch's operations.
The Operating System (OS) is saved here and loaded at each boot, so it is the software the switch runs on.
This keeps the saved startup-configuration, which holds settings rather than the software for operations.
This is the running memory the loaded contents go into, not the component that keeps them saved.

questions.stem: Right after a switch boots up, MSgt Rush types new settings into it. The file holding them sits in the switch's working memory until he backs it up. Which file holds his new settings?

keywords.text: sits in the switch's working memory

answers.rationale: This file holds saved settings in long term storage, but the file here sits in working memory.
These routines run at boot up from another component; they do not hold settings typed in.
The file in working memory that stores configuration changes until they are backed up is this one.
This software also runs in working memory, but it is not a file that holds typed settings.

questions.stem: Each time a switch powers on, MSgt Rush's team relies on one saved file kept in long-term storage. It is loaded into working memory and holds every setting specific to that switch. Which file is it?

answers.rationale: This holds the switch's settings, but it sits in working memory, while this file is kept in long-term storage.
The saved file in long-term storage, loaded at each boot with that switch's whole set of settings, is this one.
The system software is also loaded at boot, but it does not hold the settings specific to one switch.
These routines run at power-on, but they are not a file loaded into working memory with settings.

questions.stem: An airman's network mixes switches from several vendors. For network monitoring applications, he wants each device to advertise its management address, system name and port details to the devices directly connected to it. Which choice does this?

answers.rationale: This also advertises details to neighbors, but it is Cisco proprietary, and these switches come from several vendors.
This works between directly connected devices, but it detects one-way traffic rather than advertising device details.
A vendor-neutral way for devices to advertise their details to adjacent nodes, used for network monitoring, fits every fact.
This works across vendors to prevent loops; it is not used to feed network monitoring applications.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush inspects a trunk between two older Cisco devices. Each frame crossing it is tagged to identify its specific traffic, and each existing frame is wrapped inside a new outer frame. Which method is in use?

answers.rationale: Cisco-only trunk tagging that wraps the existing frame in a new header and trailer is this method.
This also tags frames on trunks, but it uses the frame as it is, without a new header and trailer.
This wraps packets in frames between two devices, but it does not tag trunk traffic to identify it.
This runs between Cisco neighbors to share details; it does not tag each frame on a trunk.

questions.stem: An airman puts a new Layer 2 switch into service, and one record in it starts out empty. As attached devices send frames, the switch fills that record on its own. Later frames leave only by the interface the record lists. Which record is this?

answers.rationale: This file holds settings typed in by a person; it is not filled by attached devices sending frames.
This file holds saved settings for boot; it does not steer later frames to an interface.
A record that starts empty, fills as devices send frames and steers later frames is this one.
A routing table belongs to a Layer 3 router, but this is a Layer 2 switch.

questions.stem: An airman joins two network devices from different vendors directly over one link and needs a way to establish communication between them. The sending device wraps each network-level packet in a Data-Link frame. Which choice fits?

answers.rationale: This adds a header and trailer to frames, but it works only with Cisco devices, and these come from different vendors.
A direct link between two devices from different vendors that frames each network-level packet fits all facts.
This shares details between neighbors; it does not wrap packets in frames.
This watches a link for one-way traffic and shuts a port; it does not establish communication between devices.

questions.stem: An airman finds that the wall jack at his desk is cabled to one switch interface, and the switch's membership list shows that interface in a single Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN). The switch forwards Sales VLAN frames out of that interface. Which kind of switch interface is it?

answers.rationale: A trunk port carries several groups, but the membership list shows this interface in a single group.
A tagged port is a trunk, typically switch to switch, but this interface is cabled to the wall jack at his desk.
An interface with one group membership that serves a desk and forwards that group's frames fits this role.
An unused port should be shut down in an inactive group, but the switch forwards Sales frames out of this one.

questions.stem: An airman creates group 99 on the base switches and gives it an Internet Protocol (IP) address so the switches can be reached remotely with Telnet. Group 99 also carries syslog messages from the switches to a logging server. Which group is 99?

answers.rationale: The default group carries the switches' own in-band traffic at first, but this group was created by the airman as group 99.
An inactive group holds shut-down unused ports, but this group lets the switches be reached remotely with Telnet.
The Sales group carries user traffic, but this group carries syslog messages from the switches to a logging server.
A created group with an address for remote Telnet access and syslog messages serves switch administration.

questions.stem: A Sales computer on one switch sends data to a Sales computer on a second switch, and the data crosses the cable between the switches along with Marketing and Research traffic. The two switches come from different major manufacturers. As the data leaves the first switch onto that cable, which step happens?

answers.rationale: The tag is removed where a frame reaches an access port, but this data is only leaving the first switch.
Data leaving a switch onto a cable shared by several groups gets marked so the far switch knows its group.

answers.text: Adds a new header and trailer
answers.rationale: Adding a new header and trailer is the Cisco-only method, but these switches come from different major manufacturers.
A Layer 3 routing process links different groups, but this data goes from one Sales computer to another.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must pass the traffic of 15 Virtual Local Area Networks (VLANs) between two switches while giving up only one interface on each switch. The switches must leave each frame as it is and add only a tag that names its VLAN. Which choice should he set up between the switches?

answers.rationale: One connection that carries all 15 groups and only tags each frame is what this setup needs.
An access port belongs to only one group, so it cannot pass the traffic of 15 groups.
EtherChannel uses more than one link, but he may give up only one interface on each switch.
This Cisco method adds a new header and trailer, but these switches must leave each frame as it is.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush moves a printer cable from interface 3 to interface 7 on the same switch, and the printer now gets Research group broadcasts where it used to get Sales group broadcasts. Interface 7 links only to the printer, and an airman set it up last week. Which setting on interface 7 places the printer in the Research group?

answers.rationale: Frame tagging marks frames crossing a trunk, but interface 7 links only to the printer, where tags are removed.
An untagged port serves one end device, but interfaces 3 and 7 are both such ports and still differ in group.
The group assigned to a physical interface decides its forwarding and filtering, so moving the cable changed the printer's group.
A trunking ID travels on frames across a trunk, but interface 7 links only to the printer.

questions.stem: A security review flags one group on a base switch network. Administrators reach the switches remotely over this group, every unused port on the switches sits in it, and the user computers on the floor sit in it too. Which group did the review flag?

answers.rationale: The group that holds every port from day one and serves in-band management may span the network if not pruned.
A management group gives administrators remote access, but this group also holds every unused port.
An inactive group holds unused, shut-down ports, but user computers on the floor sit in this group.
The Sales group holds user computers, but administrators also reach the switches remotely over this group.

questions.stem: An airman joins a Cisco switch to a switch from another major manufacturer with one cable. Sales and Research traffic must both cross that cable, and Sales computers on either switch must share broadcasts with each other. Which choice should he use on the cable?

answers.rationale: This Cisco proprietary method only works with Cisco devices, but the second switch comes from another major manufacturer.
This open standard works with all major manufacturers' models and lets several groups share one cable.
An access port is a member of only one group, but Sales and Research traffic must both cross this cable.
A Layer 3 routing process links different groups, but these Sales computers share broadcasts within one group.

questions.stem: An airman sets up a new workstation on a base subnet so it can reach remote networks. He enters one address on the workstation so its traffic can leave the local segment, and he takes it from the router interface that sits on the workstation's own subnet. Which setting is he entering?

keywords.text: router interface that sits on the workstation's own subnet

answers.rationale: A default route also leads toward unknown networks, but it is a router entry, while this address is entered on the workstation.
The workstation's own logical address identifies it, but the address here belongs to the router interface on its subnet.
Hosts use the nearest router interface on their own subnet as their path to leave the local network.
A routing table holds many network paths inside a router, while this is one address entered on the workstation.

questions.stem: An airman follows a packet that several routers forward correctly before a routing mistake bounces it between two routers. After many more trips, one of those two routers discards it while it is still being routed through the network. Which header field caused the discard?

answers.rationale: A wrong version number gets a packet discarded at once, but several routers forwarded this packet correctly first.
Routers discard packets they hold no table listing for, but these two routers kept forwarding this one many times.
The offset helps a receiving computer put fragments in order; it plays no part in a router discarding a packet.
This header counter expires when a packet is routed for too long, and the router holding it then discards the packet.

questions.stem: A router with three interfaces carries three of these values, one unique to each interface, while a host with a single connection carries one. A host learns a neighbor's value by mapping it from a known Layer 3 value. To send data off its local network, a host addresses it to its router's value of this kind. Which kind of value is this?

answers.rationale: Layer 2 values unique to each interface, learned by mapping from Layer 3 and used to reach the router, fit every fact.
Each interface also has a logical value, but data leaving a local network keeps the far host's logical value as its destination.
Address resolution is the mapping process a host runs, not a value that each interface carries.
A default gateway is a Layer 3 value set on a host, while these values are learned by mapping from Layer 3.

questions.stem: When one connection on a router fails, that router alone sends a small message describing the condition of its own connections. Every router that receives it copies the details for its own use and at once resends it through its other interfaces, until every router in the area has it. Afterward, all routers in the area hold identical topology tables. Which message did the router send?

keywords.text: describing the condition of its own connections

answers.rationale: A routing update sends a whole table only to directly connected neighbors, while this message reaches every router in the area.
Hello packets acquire neighbors and act as a keep-alive, but they do not build identical topology tables across an area.
A router advertisement is one of the messages sent back to a source about processing, not details every router copies and resends.
Only the affected router sends it, every router copies and resends it, and the area ends with identical topology tables.

questions.stem: A router holds a list in its Random Access Memory (RAM) that pairs each known destination network with a next hop. Part of the list comes from the subnets on its own interfaces, and the rest from networks learned from other routers. For each arriving packet, the router uses only the best entry to each destination. Which list is this?

keywords.text: pairs each known destination network with a next hop

answers.rationale: A topology table also holds routes learned from neighbors, but it keeps every advertised route, including backups.
A neighbor table lists each neighbor's address and interface, not networks taken from the router's own interface subnets.
The running configuration also sits in that memory, but it holds current settings, not destination and next-hop pairs.
Destination and next-hop pairs built from interface subnets and learned networks, keeping the best paths, fit this list.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush needs his base's routers to share routes with another base, which runs under its own routing policy. The routers involved must learn and track far more routes than routers inside one base, and he must define each neighbor by hand. Which choice fits this need?

answers.rationale: These route information inside one base's networks and find neighbors automatically, while these routes go to another base.
Routing between separate routing systems needs these, which track more routes and use neighbors defined by hand.
Routed protocols are the messages that get delivered; they do not learn and track routes between routers.
Link state protocols find neighbors automatically with hello packets, but here each neighbor must be defined by hand.

questions.stem: An airman links his base's border router to a router at another base so they can share routes. He defines the neighbor by hand, and the two routers open a connection-oriented session. Every update sent between them is acknowledged, and periodic keep-alives hold the session up. Which choice provides that session and the acknowledgments?

answers.rationale: This routing protocol sends the updates between bases, but it relies on another protocol for the session and acknowledgments.
This protocol gives connectionless, best-effort delivery, while this exchange runs over a connection-oriented session.
Reliable, acknowledged updates over a connection-oriented session between neighbors defined by hand fit this protocol.
Hello packets act as keep-alives and find neighbors automatically, while this neighbor was defined by hand.

questions.stem: An airman's workstation once sent a request to every device on its segment and saved the router's hardware value, matched to a distant host's logical value. Since then, each frame for that host goes straight to the router, with no new request. Which item on the workstation does it check before sending each of those frames?

keywords.text: each frame for that host goes straight to the router

answers.rationale: The workstation saved the learned match in this memory, so later frames reuse it with no new broadcast request.
The default gateway names the router's logical value, while this item matched a hardware value to a distant host.
A routing table is kept in routers and built from learned networks, not from one broadcast request on the segment.
The startup configuration holds a router's saved settings, not hardware values a workstation learned for its frames.

questions.stem: An airman suspects a host on a distant network is down. She sends a request to the host's logical address, and the host sends a reply straight back to her, which shows the two Network Layers can reach each other. The test checks nothing above the Network Layer. Which test did she run?

keywords.text: host sends a reply straight back to her

answers.rationale: A request to a destination's logical address answered by a reply, testing only Network Layer to Network Layer, fits this test.
This protocol's request and reply also map a logical address, but only for a host on the same segment.
This message reports a failed delivery from a router, while here the host itself replied to her request.
Hello packets are exchanged automatically between neighboring devices at set intervals, not sent by her to one distant host.

questions.stem: An airman follows data across an internetwork at the Network Layer. On one link with a smaller maximum message size, each packet is split into smaller pieces, and each piece gets its own copy of the header. The packets travel with best-effort delivery. Which choice is handling this data?

keywords.text: each packet is split into smaller pieces

answers.rationale: This protocol breaks a data stream into pieces at the Transport Layer, while this data is handled at the Network Layer.
This Network Layer protocol reports errors about packet processing; it does not split packets into pieces for a link.
This protocol maps a logical address to a hardware address; it does not deliver packets across an internetwork.
Best-effort delivery with fragmentation at the Network Layer matches the primary routed protocol here.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush maps the networks of one Air Force Base, which its network teams run under a common administration with a single, clearly defined routing strategy. Inside, the networks are split into groups of contiguous networks, one of which links all the others. The base as a whole is assigned its own number for use in Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) routing. Which term names the base's whole set of networks?

answers.rationale: A group of networks under one administration with a single clearly defined routing policy, numbered for routing between bases, fits all facts.
Areas are the groups of contiguous networks inside the base, not the whole base that gets its own routing number.
The backbone is the one area that links all other areas, not the base's whole set of networks.
Any networks joined by routers form an internetwork, but one routing strategy and a routing number mark a more specific term.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush watches his base's routers exchange updates with each other at regular intervals and learn about networks they are not directly connected to. Each router applies metric costs to the paths it learns and keeps the best one in its table. When an update reports a change, the routers rerun their algorithms and replace the old entries. What are the routers using?

answers.rationale: A default route is a single manual path for unknown destinations, so it applies no metric costs to learned paths.
Static routes stay as entered until changed by hand, so they would not be recalculated when an update reports a change.
Hello messages acquire neighbors and act as a keep-alive, but they do not teach routers about distant networks.
Exchanging updates, learning remote networks, applying metric costs and recalculating after changes is dynamic learning by these protocols.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush watches a router take in data on one interface and read its Layer 3 destination. Finding a matching entry, the router writes its outbound interface's hardware address as the frame's source and the next hop's as its destination, then sends it on. The Layer 3 source and destination stay exactly as they were. Which router function is he watching?

answers.rationale: Forwarding data from interface to interface while hardware addresses change and Layer 3 addresses stay fixed fits this function.
Choosing the route comes before this step; here the router is moving the frame out with rewritten hardware addresses.
Address resolution maps a logical address to a hardware address, but here data arriving on an interface is forwarded on.
Neighbor discovery identifies nearby devices with hello messages, while here a table entry is matched and data forwarded.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush plugs a leased line from a distant base straight into a router. The connection must be configured before it works, and it then carries the two bases' daily data traffic. Which connection on the router is he using?

keywords.text: leased line from a distant base

answers.rationale: Ethernet interfaces are configured too, but they connect the router to a local network, not a line from a distant base.
A configured connection carrying data over a long-distance line between bases fits the router's wide area links.
The console connection works without any configuration, while this connection had to be configured before it worked.
The auxiliary connection reaches a distant modem for remote setup, not the daily data traffic between two bases.

questions.stem: An airman types one entry into a small branch router so that traffic for a single remote office network always leaves through the same interface. When a link on that path fails, the entry stays exactly as he typed it until he edits it. Packets for every other unknown network are discarded. Which kind of entry did he create?

answers.rationale: A default route would give packets for unknown networks a way out, yet those packets are discarded here.
An entry typed by hand for one network that changes only when edited matches the manually configured kind.
A learned entry would be recalculated by routing software after the link failure, but this one stayed as typed.
A backup route is chosen by a routing protocol from its topology table, while this entry was typed in.

questions.stem: A base edge router lists only a few internal networks in its table. An airman hand-enters one entry in that router's own table so that packets for every network missing from the table go on to the provider's router, which has more detailed entries. Which entry did he add?

keywords.text: every network missing from the table

answers.rationale: A backup route serves a destination already known in the topology table, but these packets have no known destination.
A default gateway is the router address set on hosts to leave a network, not an entry in the router's own table.
A hand-entered catch-all entry that sends every unknown destination on to a better-informed router fits all the facts.
Learned entries come from routing protocol updates, but this entry was entered by hand.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush compares how his routers rate two paths to a file server. The routers work each rating out themselves, and a path's rating is the same at midnight as at peak hours. The path over two routers and slow leased lines rates better than the path over five routers and Ethernet links. Which metric gives this rating?

answers.rationale: Delay depends on port queues and congestion, so this rating would change between midnight and peak hours.
Bandwidth rates a link's traffic capacity, so the path over Ethernet links would rate better.
Reliability ratings are values usually assigned to links by network administrators, not worked out by routers.
A rating the routers work out from the routers a packet crosses, steady at any hour, fits every fact.

questions.stem: An airman gives each link in her network a number she chooses herself, and the routers compare these numbers to pick paths. A microwave link that fails often in storms and takes a day to repair gets a poor number. A buried fiber link that seldom goes down gets a good one, even when the microwave link sits idle. What is she setting?

answers.rationale: A number an administrator assigns to rate how often a link fails and how fast it is repaired is this metric.
Reliable service is an internetworking challenge of consistent access, not a number routers compare to pick paths.
Communication cost is also set by the administrator, but it rates operating expense, not storm failures and repair time.
Load rates how busy a resource is, yet the fiber link wins even while the microwave link sits idle.

questions.stem: An airman watches one value her routers use to compare paths. It rises when packets wait longer in port queues at routers along the way and when links are congested. It falls when a link is upgraded to more capacity and grows with the physical distance packets must travel. Which value is this?

answers.rationale: Bandwidth is a link's capacity, which does not change with the physical distance packets travel.
A value built from queues, congestion, link capacity and distance is the time a packet takes to cross the internetwork.
Load rates how busy a resource is, which does not grow with the physical distance packets travel.
Hop count counts routers crossed and stays the same however long packets wait in port queues.

questions.stem: An airman's routing protocol prefers a 10 Mbps Ethernet link over a 64 kbps leased line, though each is a single link between the same two routers. The value it uses for the Ethernet link stays the same when that link becomes busy, so packets sometimes arrive later over it. Which value is the protocol using?

keywords.text: stays the same when that link becomes busy

answers.rationale: Hop count would rate both single links equally, yet the protocol prefers the faster link.
Delay would grow when the Ethernet link gets busy, but this value stays the same.
A rating of each link's maximum attainable throughput favors the faster link even when it is busy.
Load rises as a resource gets busier, but this value stays the same when the link is busy.

questions.stem: A link state router gives each interface a value that is larger for a slow serial link than for a fast Ethernet link. It adds the values of every interface along a path to find the total to a destination. When gigabit links began to get the same value as slower links, an airman changed the reference figure so that faster links score lower. Which value is this?

answers.rationale: Hop count adds one per router and would rate one serial link the same as one Ethernet link.
Delay is the time a packet takes to cross the internetwork, which no reference figure sets.
Bandwidth is larger for the fast Ethernet link, while this value is larger for the slow serial link.
A reference figure divided by each interface's bandwidth, summed along the path, gives this link state metric.

questions.stem: An airman sets up a small interior network whose routers are simple to configure and put little demand on their processors. Each router sends its whole table to its directly connected neighbors at regular intervals and after any change. A router accepts what its neighbors send without knowing where the information first came from. Which approach are the routers using?

answers.rationale: Simple setup, low processor demand, whole tables sent to neighbors and trusting unverified updates are the traits of routing by rumor.
Link state routers send small updates about their own links, not whole tables to neighbors.
A balanced hybrid sends smaller updates only when the topology changes, not at regular intervals.
Path vectors serve exterior routing between separately run systems, not a small interior network.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's routers need more processor power and memory than his old ones and seldom suffer routing loops. After a change, only the directly affected routers send a small multicast message, and each router that receives it copies it and resends it at once. Every router in an area can see the whole way to each destination. Which routing approach are the routers using?

answers.rationale: Distance vector routers place little demand on the processor, but these routers need more power and memory.
Higher processor and memory needs, small multicast updates resent at once and a full view of the area fit this approach.
A balanced hybrid also multicasts on changes but uses distance vectors and has no areas, so routers cannot see the whole way.
Path vectors serve exterior routing, whose updates go over acknowledged sessions rather than small multicast messages.

questions.stem: An airman's routers serve a small network inside one base. Each router sends its full table to its directly connected neighbors every 30 seconds and again right after a topology change, so news of a change reaches distant routers one router at a time. Which of these is running on the routers?

answers.rationale: This link state protocol sends small multicast advertisements about its own links, not full tables every 30 seconds.
This exterior protocol links separately run systems, such as two bases, not a small network inside one base.
Full tables to direct neighbors every 30 seconds and on changes, converging one router at a time, match this distance vector protocol.
This balanced hybrid protocol sends smaller updates only when the topology changes, not every 30 seconds.

questions.stem: Right after power-up, a link state router sends hello packets and hears back from routers on its own networks. Software on the router fills in entries automatically, one for each router it hears from. Each entry stays only while that router's hello packets show that it and the link between them still work. Where are these entries kept?

answers.rationale: A topology table holds the advertisements received from all routers in the area, and its entries do not depend on each router's hello packets.
Entries for adjacent routers found and kept alive by hello packets are what this table holds.
A routing table holds an entry per destination network with its next hop, not one per router heard from.
Hello packets are how the routers are found and kept alive, while the question asks where the resulting entries are kept.

questions.stem: After hello packets find adjacent routers, a link state router gathers every advertisement received from all routers in its group into one store. That store is identical on every router of the group. The router's calculation reads it to produce entries for a separate store used to forward packets. What is the gathering store called?

answers.rationale: A neighbor table records each adjacent router's address and interface, not every advertisement from the group.
The routing table is the separate store that forwards packets, filled from calculations on the gathered advertisements.
The overall picture of the group, holding all received advertisements and identical on each router there, is this table.
Each router builds this tree with itself as root, so it differs from router to router.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush wants routers that use distance vectors but send small multicast updates only when the topology changes, using far less bandwidth than older distance vector designs. Each router should hold a backup path in its tables so it can switch at once when the best path fails. Which choice meets his needs?

answers.rationale: This link state protocol builds a full map of its area instead of using distance vectors.
This Routing Information Protocol (RIP) version keeps only the best route in its table, so it holds no backup path to switch to.
This older distance vector protocol uses significantly more bandwidth than the one that meets these needs.
A balanced hybrid that multicasts updates on changes and keeps a feasible successor as backup meets every need.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush checks a router that runs a balanced hybrid protocol. For one specific known network, its algorithm compared the paths that neighbors advertised in the topology table and placed one of them in the routing table, where it forwards packets now. A second path waits in the topology table in case the first fails. Which name fits the path in the routing table?

answers.rationale: The best path chosen by the algorithm from the topology table and placed in the routing table carries this name.
A feasible successor is the backup that waits in the topology table until the best path fails.
A default route serves packets for unknown networks, but this path leads to one specific known network.
A static route is entered by an administrator, while this path was chosen by the algorithm from advertised paths.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's interior routers use distance vectors to pick paths, yet any topology change triggers small updates sent by multicast. Each router keeps neighbor, topology and routing tables, and the design is meant to stay simple to configure while converging fast. Which type of routing approach is this?

answers.rationale: A pure distance vector type sends broadcast updates on a schedule, not small multicast updates on each topology change.
Using distance vectors while multicasting small updates on changes combines the advantages of both main types.
A pure link state type builds a full map of the area instead of picking paths by distance vectors.
Path vectors serve exterior routing between separately run systems, not interior routers.

questions.stem: To reduce vulnerabilities on base routers, an airman downloads configuration documents from the organization that coined their name in 1998, along with a viewer. She applies their settings to lock down typically permissive software and prevent attacker access over the network, then validates each device with scanning software. What did she download?

answers.rationale: These lists are a form of logical security set on a device, not configuration documents downloaded with a viewer.
These guides are also configuration standards, but the documents here come from the organization that coined their name in 1998.
Documents from the Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) that lock down permissive software and are checked by scanning software fit every fact.
A startup-configuration file holds one router's saved settings; it is not a downloaded set of lockdown documents.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush times how many seconds pass after a link failure until every router's table reflects it. On his older network, news of the failure is passed one router at a time and takes long. On his newer network, routers with a backup path already stored finish far sooner. What is he timing?

keywords.text: until every router's table reflects it

answers.rationale: Delay is the time one packet takes from source to destination, not the time until every table reflects a failure.
Hold time is how long a router treats one neighbor as reachable, not the time for every table to update.
A stored backup route speeds things up, but it is a route, not the span of seconds being timed.
The time for news of a change to reach every router's table, slow one router at a time, is what he times.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must choose one device for a base network that gathers the links of many devices across the base and handles a large amount of traffic. He also wants it to route between Virtual Local Area Networks (VLANs) and to apply the base's address translation policies. Which device fits all of these needs?

keywords.text: gathers the links of many devices

answers.rationale: Access switches connect end user devices, but gathering the links of many devices across the base is the aggregation role one tier up.
High-speed switches suit heavy traffic, but address translation is kept off them so they can switch packets at top speed.
A firewall is one policy tool, but gathering many devices' links and routing between workgroup networks fit the aggregation point.
The aggregation point for many access switches handles heavy traffic, routes between workgroup networks and holds address translation policies.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush takes one division of a base network and breaks it into smaller divisions. He sizes each smaller division to the number of devices in its office so that fewer addresses go to waste. To get the full benefit, he moves the base routers to Open Shortest Path First (OSPF). Which approach is he using?

answers.rationale: Subnetting divides a network, but needing newer routers for the full benefit points to a design with more than one mask.
This format joins networks into larger supernets, but here one division is broken into smaller divisions.
Breaking a subnet into differently sized subnets, with newer routers for the full benefit, is this design.
Fixed length masking also breaks divisions apart, but each smaller division here is sized to its own office.

questions.stem: An airman marks each network on a base diagram with how many of its bits belong to the network. He says the same approach can join several networks into one larger network. He chose it because it carves out address blocks closer to what each office needs. Which approach is he using?

keywords.text: how many of its bits belong to the network

answers.rationale: Marking network bits, joining networks into larger ones and allocating closely to need all fit this addressing approach.
A mask also shows the network bits, but it is a value, not an approach that carves out blocks to fit each office.
A supernet is the larger network that results, not an approach for marking each network's bits.
That design also sizes blocks to need, but it breaks a subnet into further subnets.

questions.stem: An airman finds the value 255.255.255.128 listed beside a printer's Internet Protocol (IP) address as a separate entry. She learns that it marks how many bits are taken from the host part of that address. Other offices on the same network list different values beside their printers. Which item is the value beside this printer's address?

answers.rationale: A network address is also a dotted value listed with a device, but it does not mark borrowed host bits.
A separate dotted value that marks the borrowed host bits of one printer's address is that address's own mask.
That format also shows borrowed bits, but as a slash and number tacked onto the address.
That design is the network holding different values per office, not the single value beside one printer.

questions.stem: An airman divides a base network into smaller portions, one for each department, so that each department sees only its own printers. He takes bits from the host part of every address to make the portions. He expects reduced traffic and simpler management afterward, and every base router runs Routing Information Protocol (RIP) version 1. Which term names his work?

keywords.text: divides a base network into smaller portions

answers.rationale: That design also divides networks, but version 1 routers allow only one mask, so its full benefit is impossible here.
That format also counts bits taken from the host part, but it joins networks into larger supernets.
A mask marks which host bits are borrowed, but reduced traffic and simpler management are benefits of the whole process.
Dividing a network into portions by borrowing host bits, for reduced traffic and simpler management, is the process here.

questions.stem: An airman sets up a field network with a short cable supply, so he picks the layout that needs less cable than some others and is easy to configure. Each workstation taps directly into one main cable run. Midway through the exercise, one break in that run takes down every workstation at once, and he struggles to find the fault. Which physical layout did he pick?

answers.rationale: A star topology also fails as a whole when its central hub or switch fails, but its cable costs run higher.
One shared central medium needs less cable and is easy to configure, yet one break brings down the whole network and is hard to isolate.
A tree topology links star-configured segments to a backbone, but here each workstation taps directly into the main run.
This logical layout describes how data is broadcast to every device, but the question asks which physical layout he picked.

questions.stem: An airman cables a small office network, and the job uses more cable than he expected. Last week one workstation crashed while the others kept working normally. Today a single box in the wiring closet failed, and every workstation lost access at once. Which layout does the office use?

answers.rationale: In a full mesh each node links directly to every other node, so no single failure cuts off every workstation.
In a partial mesh, nodes link to the nodes they interact with most, so no single box serves every workstation.
A broken central bus also takes everyone down, but a bus is a cable, not a box, and it needs less cable, not more.
One crash spares the rest, a failed central hub or switch cuts off every node, and cable costs run higher.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush reviews the protocol that a base network's logical topology uses to define the path for packets between its switches and nodes. That protocol relies on a separate contention access method so that only one system transmits at a time. Which protocol is it?

answers.rationale: This is the contention access method that the protocol relies on, not the protocol that defines the path between switches and nodes.
Routing protocols appear on logical network diagrams, but they do not rely on a contention access method to share the cable.
This protocol defines the logical path between switches and nodes and relies on a contention access method to share the cable.
These addresses and subnets are laid out on logical diagrams, but they do not rely on a contention access method to share the cable.

questions.stem: An airman maps a base network for a new drawing. In headquarters, every workstation cables back to one switch; on the flight line, shops tap into a single cable with two ends. In the server room, each server links directly to every other server. All three areas are joined into one network, so which term names the layout of the whole network?

answers.rationale: Joining star, two-ended shared cable and full mesh areas into one network is a combination of topologies.
A tree topology joins star-configured segments to a linear bus backbone, but this network also links servers directly to each other.
Only the server room links each node to every other node, while headquarters workstations run back to one switch.
Headquarters fits a central switch layout, but the flight line shops tap into one shared cable with two ends.

questions.stem: An airman diagrams a base pay system using only four kinds of symbols. One symbol receives timecard entries and leave requests, and it sits inside the system she is mapping. What leaves it is a single pay record, which it passes straight on. Which kind of symbol is it?

answers.rationale: A data store holds data that is not moving, but this symbol passes its record straight on.
A data flow is the movement of data itself, but this symbol receives two inputs and sends out a different record.
An external entity lies outside the system boundary, but this symbol sits inside the system being mapped.
Receiving entries and requests and sending out a single pay record inside the system transforms incoming data into outgoing data.

questions.stem: An airman models a unit's supply records system with only four kinds of symbols. Her chart shows every path that information could take through the system. She can redraw any part at a lower level with more detail, like finding the Chicago streets on a state road map. Which chart is she making?

answers.rationale: A context diagram uses the same symbols, but it is only the top level, Level 0, not a chart redrawn at lower levels.
A logical network diagram also shows how information flows, but with subnets, routers and routing protocols, not only four symbols.
Four symbols, every possible path, and more detail on lower hierarchical levels, like a road map, describe this chart.
A physical network diagram gives a floorplan view of cables and hardware, not every path that information could take.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush prepares a drawing for the wing's troubleshooting binder. It marks each router and firewall that the wing operates. It also traces the way information travels among those devices from one end of the base to the other. Which drawing is he preparing?

answers.rationale: A drawing that describes the way information flows and shows devices like routers and firewalls fits every fact here.
A physical network diagram shows the arrangement of cables and hardware, but it does not trace how information travels.
A data flow diagram uses only four symbols to represent a system, so it does not mark routers and firewalls.
A context diagram is the top level of a data flow diagram, built from the same four symbols, with no routers or firewalls.

questions.stem: An airman's office cables every workstation back to one switch. He then writes a separate record of how data moves across those nodes. He will use that record as a blueprint to help implement the next network physically. Which term names what his record describes?

answers.rationale: A star topology describes how workstations are cabled to a central switch, not how data moves across the nodes.
How data moves across the nodes, used as a blueprint to help implement the network physically, describes this type.
Physical topology is the interconnection of devices that the blueprint helps build, not the record of how data moves.
A data flow diagram is like a road map of all data paths, not a blueprint used to build a network physically.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush is developing a floorplan-style drawing for a new building's Ethernet segment that shows each run's cable type and length. Before he finalizes it, he checks those runs against a published source. That same source also covers the connector types for the fiber runs. Which does he check the runs against?

answers.rationale: A physical network diagram is the drawing that shows the runs, not the published source he checks them against.
These are utilized when developing diagrams to ensure the proper cable type and distance, and they cover connector types.
This access method governs how devices on an Ethernet segment contend to transmit, not cable types or connectors.
A procedure specification details the steps of a specific task, not cable type, distance or connector types.

questions.stem: An airman connects four computers to an old device, and every message one computer sends comes out of all the device's other interfaces. Which device is she using?

keywords.text: comes out of all the device's other interfaces

answers.rationale: Repeating every message out all other interfaces is how this legacy device works.
A switch sends each message only to the device it was meant for.
A router is a Layer 3 device that forwards packets between networks.
A Layer 3 switch combines switching and routing, so it reads addresses before sending.

questions.stem: An airman reads that a switch learns and forms multiple internal connections in hardware to pass or filter traffic. Which hardware makes this possible?

answers.rationale: This memory keeps saved startup settings; it does not form internal connections.
This is running memory for current settings, not the hardware that forms connections.
This memory holds diagnostic and boot up routines, not connection hardware.
These circuits let switches learn and form many internal connections to pass or filter traffic.

questions.stem: When an airman plugs a printer into a switch, the switch tells it apart from every other device by a fixed 48-bit number. Which identifier is this?

answers.rationale: Each device is identified to the switch by this 48-bit identifier.
A logical address is assigned for remote configuration, not a fixed 48-bit device number.
An interface ID names the switch port, not the printer itself.
A system name is a detail that discovery protocols advertise, not a 48-bit number.

questions.stem: An airman must name the standard that the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) created to prevent bridging loops in data networks. Which standard is it?

answers.rationale: This standard tags frames crossing trunks; it does not prevent bridging loops.
This standard was created to prevent bridging loops and provide loop-free topologies.
This is a Cisco proprietary trunking protocol, not a standard for loops.
This feature shuts a port when traffic flows one way; it is not the bridging standard.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush wants bad frames thrown away at the switch so the traffic it sends on is as error-free as possible. Which switching method should he choose?

answers.rationale: This method sends bad frames on, leaving the destination to ask for a resend.
This method discards bad frames, which ensures a high level of error-free traffic.
This method checks only the first 64 bytes of each frame.
This picks a method from traffic conditions rather than always discarding bad frames.

questions.stem: An airman reviews an outage in which every link was swamped after devices kept resending the same data to every device. The causes included low port rate switches and improper network configurations. Which problem occurred?

answers.rationale: This is one device getting the same frame from several segments, confusing the table.
Swamped links from data resent to every device, with these listed causes, describe this problem.
This is loops inside other loops, a layout rather than these listed causes.
A late collision is a transmission after another host's first 64 bytes.

questions.stem: An airman adds redundant links between switches and must apply the standardized solution for avoiding the loops this creates. Which choice is that solution?

answers.rationale: This feature shuts a port when traffic flows in one direction.
This protocol advertises configurations to neighbors.
This protocol lets devices learn about neighboring Cisco devices.
This is the standardized solution for avoiding loops between switches.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush wants a hybrid method that checks more than the fastest method does, yet sends sooner than one holding each entire frame. Which switching method fits?

answers.rationale: This hybrid of the other two checks only the first 64 bytes before sending.
This method holds each entire frame before sending.
This is the fastest method, copying only the destination address.
This selects a method based on traffic conditions rather than mixing two.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush splits one large flat network into five Virtual Local Area Networks (VLANs) because hello packets from thousands of computers cause bandwidth issues. What does each of the five VLANs now form?

answers.rationale: A trunk link carries several groups between switches; it is not what each group forms.
One group can span several physical segments, so each group is not one segment.
Each group keeps its broadcasts from the others, so each forms its own broadcast domain.
An access port is one switch port for an end device, not what each group forms.

questions.stem: An airman finds that the trunking method on an old base cable is deprecated and runs only between Cisco devices. Which method is it?

answers.rationale: 802.1q is an open standard that works with all major manufacturers' models.
This Cisco protocol is untagged device traffic that switches send on group 1, not a trunking method.
This protocol is untagged device traffic on group 1, not a trunking method.
This deprecated Cisco proprietary method for trunks only works with Cisco devices.

questions.stem: As traffic crosses a trunk, an airman sees the Sales Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) marked 10, Marketing 20 and Research 30, and the far switch reads each mark to find its VLAN. Which process is this?

answers.rationale: Placing a trunking ID on each piece of traffic so the far switch can match its group is this process.
A switchport membership is set on a physical port, not marked on traffic crossing a trunk.
A trunking ID is the mark itself, while the question asks for the process that places it.
A Layer 3 routing process carries traffic between groups, not marks traffic inside one trunk.

questions.stem: An airman uses routers to join lines from three separate base networks so that hosts on each can reach the others. What is the joined whole called?

answers.rationale: A broadcast domain is the set of devices that all see each broadcast, not separate networks joined by routers.
A collision domain is a segment where frames can collide, not separate networks joined by routers.
Routers that connect lines from different networks create an internetwork, which is what the joined base networks are.
A subnet is one part of a single network, not several separate networks joined by routers.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must pick how routes are shared among the routers inside his own base, following a single routing policy. Which group should he choose from?

answers.rationale: These route between separate bases with their own policies, not among routers inside one base.
These protocols are designed to route information within one connected group of networks, such as one base.
Path vector protocols carry routes between separate routing systems, such as between bases, not inside one base.
Routed protocols are the messages that get delivered; they do not share routes among routers.

questions.stem: A host asks every device on its segment for the Media Access Control (MAC) value of a host on another segment, and the router answers with its own MAC value. Which request did the router answer?

keywords.text: the router answers with its own MAC value

answers.rationale: The router acts as a proxy, answering this resolution request with its own hardware value for the remote host.
This protocol reports packet processing errors back to a source; it does not answer requests for hardware values.
Hello packets let neighbors learn about each other at intervals; they are not single requests for one host's value.
This protocol acknowledges messages in a connection-oriented session; it does not ask for hardware values.

questions.stem: A router receives a packet for a network missing from its table, yet it still sends the packet toward another router that may know more. Which table entry did it use?

keywords.text: a network missing from its table

answers.rationale: A successor is the best path to a known network, but this network is missing from the table.
A feasible successor is a backup path to a known network, but this network is missing from the table.
A dynamic route is a learned path to a known network, but this network is missing from the table.
This gateway of last resort sends packets for unknown networks toward another router.

questions.stem: An airman pings a working host on a distant network. Which message does the host send back to her computer?

answers.rationale: The echo request is the message that goes out to the destination, not the one that comes back.
A destination that receives the echo request responds with this message.
This message reports a failed delivery; this working host was reached.
This message is about a router, not a host's answer to a ping.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must share routes between his base's network and another base's network, each run with its own clearly defined routing policy, keeping every chosen path free of loops. Which choice fits?

answers.rationale: Exchanging routes between separately run systems with loop-free path selection is the exterior protocol's main function.
This interior link state protocol routes within one system's areas, not between two bases.
This interior balanced hybrid protocol routes inside one system, not between two separately run bases.
This interior distance vector protocol routes inside one system using hop count.

questions.stem: An airman's routers rate each path by its up-time, its capacity and how busy it is, then combine these values to choose the best path. What are these values called?

answers.rationale: Routing tables store the chosen best paths; they are not the up-time and capacity values being compared.
Up-time, capacity and busyness are reliability, bandwidth and load, which algorithms use to pick the best path.
Administrative distance ranks how trustworthy a routing source is, not a path's up-time or capacity.
Routing updates are messages routers exchange, not values that rate a path's up-time or capacity.

questions.stem: An airman's routers rate each router by its Central Processing Unit (CPU) utilization and packets processed per second. Which metric do these figures measure?

answers.rationale: Delay is the time a packet takes to cross the internetwork, not a router's processor use.
Bandwidth is a link's available traffic capacity, not how hard a router's processor works.
Processor utilization and packets processed per second are ways to calculate how busy a router is.
Reliability rates a link's dependability, such as its bit-error rate, not a router's processing.

questions.stem: Which of these has two primary types, distance vector and link state, each with a different impact on network and router resources?

answers.rationale: Routing tables hold the chosen paths; they are not split into distance vector and link state types.
Routed protocols provide logical addressing for packets; they are not path-calculation types.
Routing metrics are values such as hop count and delay, not types of path calculation.
Distance vector and link state are the two primary types of these formulas, each using resources differently.

questions.stem: On a link state router, which algorithm builds a tree with the router itself as the root for each known subnetwork?

answers.rationale: This algorithm finds best and backup routes for a balanced hybrid protocol, not a tree on a link state router.
Distance vector algorithms build tables from neighbors' tables rather than a tree with the router as root.
From the topology table, each link state router runs this algorithm to build a tree rooted at itself.
Path vectors are route attributes for exterior routing policy, not a tree-building algorithm.

questions.stem: An Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP) router stores every destination advertised by its neighbors, with each neighbor's advertised metric. Where does it store them?

keywords.text: every destination advertised by its neighbors

answers.rationale: The neighbor table records each discovered neighbor's address and interface, not every advertised destination.
The routing table holds only the best routes pulled from where all advertised destinations are kept.
This cache maps network addresses to physical addresses, not advertised destinations and metrics.
Every destination advertised by neighbors, with each advertised metric, is kept in this table.

questions.stem: An airman runs a small network with a simple design and predictable traffic, and wants entries that help control security and reduce traffic. Which choice fits these needs?

answers.rationale: Hand-entered routes are simple to configure, suit predictable traffic and help control security and reduce traffic.
Dynamic routes recalculate through routing protocols, which suits large, diverse, changing networks more than this one.
A successor is the best route a balanced hybrid protocol picks, not a simple hand-entered entry.
A feasible successor is a balanced hybrid protocol's backup route, not a simple hand-entered entry.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush wants a simple protocol that uses distance vectors and a 15-hop limit, but his subnets use masks of different lengths. Which version meets both needs?

answers.rationale: The original version leaves subnet mask information out of its updates, so masks of different lengths fail.
This version keeps the 15-hop distance vector design and adds mask data to updates for different mask lengths.
This balanced hybrid protocol uses bandwidth and delay as metrics, not a hop count with a 15-hop limit.
This link state protocol uses a cost metric based on bandwidth, not a hop count limit.

questions.stem: Distance vector algorithms are described as unsuitable for large networks because they are limited by which value?

answers.rationale: Bandwidth is a link capacity, not the stated limit that makes these algorithms unsuitable for large networks.
Delay is a packet's travel time, not the stated limit of distance vector algorithms.
Load is how busy a resource is, not the stated limit of distance vector algorithms.
Distance vector algorithms are limited by the number of devices crossed, which makes them unsuitable for large networks.

questions.stem: An airman's file request must reach a server at a remote site. Which tier handles that remote-service traffic, finds the best path and then forwards the request for transport?

answers.rationale: The core transports the request after the best path is found, but it does not choose that path.
The access layer delivers frames to end user computers; remote-service traffic is handled one tier up.
All traffic for remote services is handled here, and after finding the best path it forwards the request onward.
Data Link names technologies for speed and redundancy, not a tier of the three-layer model that picks paths.

questions.stem: On a base diagram, an airman labels one network with a single entry: 205.112.45.60/25. Which format is she using?

answers.rationale: A mask listed by itself is a separate value such as 255.255.255.128, not tacked onto the address.
An address with the number of mask bits after a slash is the network/mask format.
That scheme gives a network more than one mask; it is not a way of labeling one address.
A supernet is a larger network made by joining networks, not a way of writing an address.

questions.stem: An airman sketches which device each cable connects to in a small office, like a bird's eye floorplan. Which kind of layout is he sketching?

answers.rationale: Logical topology is how data moves through the network, bound to protocols, not which device each cable reaches.
Which device each cable connects to is the interconnection of network devices, drawn like a floorplan.
A logical bus topology describes data broadcast to the whole network, not the cabling between devices.
A data flow diagram uses four symbols for data paths, not the cables between office devices.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush watches the stations on his segment listen to the cable and compete for each chance to transmit data. Which network technology works this way?

keywords.text: compete for each chance to transmit

answers.rationale: Routing protocols appear on logical network diagrams; they are not the technology whose stations compete to transmit.
These addresses are laid out on logical network diagrams; they do not make stations compete to transmit.
A logical bus topology is how data is broadcast, not the network technology whose stations compete to transmit.
This contention-based network technology has devices compete for the right to transmit data.

questions.stem: An airman's four-symbol model of a billing system must show invoices moving from the ordering step to the billing step. Which entity shows that movement?

answers.rationale: The movement of data in the system, such as invoices passing between steps, is shown by this entity.
Processes transform incoming data into outgoing data, so the ordering and billing steps themselves are processes.
Data stores are repositories for data that is not moving, but these invoices are moving.
External entities are sources or destinations outside the system boundary, not movement between steps inside it.

questions.stem: An airman replaces an old device whose computers all shared bandwidth with one whose ports each give one computer bandwidth it uses alone. What does each new port form?

answers.rationale: Broadcasts still reach every port of the new device, so a port is not its own broadcast area.
A port whose bandwidth serves one computer alone forms its own separate area for collisions.
A trunk carries tagged frames between switches, not one computer's traffic on its own port.
A loop is more than one path to the same destination, not a single port.

questions.stem: On core links an airman sets switches to send each frame on after reading only its destination, so little time passes between arrival and departure. Which benefit does she gain?

keywords.text: little time passes between arrival and departure

answers.rationale: Sending after reading only the destination lets bad frames through, so traffic is not kept error-free.
Broadcast control comes from segmenting networks into smaller broadcast domains.
Reading only the destination before sending keeps the lag through the switch small.
Low cost compares a switch price with its many ports, not how fast frames leave.
