Two guests on separate hardware that both carry traffic daily, so one lost host does not stop the service, show this use.
This plan responds to catastrophes, but here both guests carried traffic every normal day and absorbed one lost host.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must add a second router to the unit's live network while saving the purchase, power and upkeep of another physical box. The router that his guest virtual server connects through exists only in software on the host. Which approach is he using?

answers.rationale: Development and Testing recreates devices in a sandbox for trials, but this router serves the unit's live network.
Para-Virtualization gives a guest access to real server equipment, but this router exists only in software.
Operating-System-Level Virtualization runs containers on the host's kernel, but here a guest virtual server uses the router.
A router that exists only in software, presented to a guest virtual server, saves buying, powering and maintaining a real one.

questions.stem: On a host running Windows Server, an airman installs a hypervisor on top and creates guests that each run their own full system. To speed up software processing, he changes the setup so the software inside each guest gains some direct access to the real server equipment. Which architecture is he using?

answers.rationale: Hardware Emulation presents mimicked devices to guests, so the software inside would not touch the real server equipment.
Full guests above a hypervisor whose software gains some access to real hardware, streamlining processing, match this architecture.
Operating-System-Level Virtualization uses containers on a shared kernel, but here each guest runs its own full system.
A Type 1 Hypervisor sits on bare hardware in place of Windows Server, but here Windows Server runs underneath.

questions.stem: A squadron relies on an old logistics program that works only on a legacy system, while every workstation must keep its new, fully patched system. An airman sets up the program on a central server. Dozens of airmen now use it at the same time from their own devices. Which approach is she using?

answers.rationale: A centrally run program reached by many users lets old software run in a foreign environment while workstations stay patched.
Hardware Emulation mimics a device for a guest server; it does not let dozens of airmen share one program at once.
User Profile Virtualization moves a user's settings and data between devices; it does not keep an old program running.
Server Virtualization partitions a server into virtual servers; it does not let workstations keep a new system while using old software.

questions.stem: During a routine budget review, a wing finds thirty single-job machines that each sat mostly idle. An airman turns them into guests that now run on three physical hosts, and she assigns each guest to a host herself. The wing now has far fewer machines to maintain. Which application of virtualization is this?

answers.rationale: Server Pooling lets software choose the best host for each guest, but here the airman chose every host herself.
Load Balancing puts idle guests to work sharing a workload, but this move left the wing far fewer machines to maintain.
Moving many idle, single-job machines onto a few hosts raises utilization and cuts the number of machines to maintain.
This plan responds to catastrophes such as a lost data center, not to a routine budget review.

questions.stem: An airman's team keeps the host system, every guest system and the hypervisor current with each vendor release, doing all work in approved windows after staging tests. Months after its maker put out a newer release closing a critical flaw, a small open-source library in the guests' admin console still runs its original version. Which security area needs attention?

answers.rationale: Change Control was followed with staging tests and approved windows; the gap is a component that missed its maker's newer release.
Asset Tracking and Management keeps inventories and watches vulnerability news, but the gap is a small library never brought up to date.
Logging and Auditing records who did what in the environment; it would not have brought the small library up to date.
Big targets were kept current while a small open-source component was forgotten, the gap this area warns about.

questions.stem: An airman's Apple laptop came with Apple's own software, which runs his mail and browser every day. He installs VMware Fusion on top of that software, which keeps handling the laptop's hardware drivers, and builds a Windows 10 guest beside his Apple apps. Which term names Apple's own software in this setup?

answers.rationale: A Type 2 Hypervisor such as VMware Fusion is what he installs on top; the question asks about the software beneath it.
The software the laptop came with, which the hosted hypervisor runs on top of and which supplies the drivers, is the base layer.
The machine he builds holds the Windows 10 guest; it is not the software the laptop came with.
A container must match the software it runs on, so it could not hold the Windows 10 guest, and it is not the base layer.

questions.stem: An airman builds a guest that has its own Basic Input/Output System (BIOS), disks, memory and processors and runs its own copy of Windows Server 2022. It shares one physical computer with five others like it, yet to users it behaves just like a stand-alone computer. Which term names what he built?

answers.rationale: A container shares its base system's kernel and carries no separate copy of Windows Server of its own.
Windows Server 2022 is only the guest system inside; the airman built the whole guest with its own disks and memory.
Software and its own system, tricked into thinking it has dedicated hardware while sharing it, behaves like a physical computer.
The host server is the shared physical computer underneath, not one of the six guests that share it.

questions.stem: Members of an airman's flight log in from any thin device and see their own full workstation with all of their programs. The heavy work runs in isolated environments on central hardware, which has cut his admin workload. Which type is this?

answers.rationale: Server Virtualization partitions a physical server into virtual servers for clients, not a full workstation for each member.
Application Virtualization serves single programs from a central server, but these members get a workstation with all their programs.
User Profile Virtualization moves profile settings and data between devices; it does not run the work in isolated central environments.
A full workstation reached from any device, with its work isolated on central hardware, separates it from the device and eases administration.

questions.stem: Under a tight budget, a wing wants its existing machines kept far busier, software that picks the best machine for each new workload so admins stop hunting, and mission systems running again quickly at another site after a catastrophe. Which approach gives the wing all three?

answers.rationale: Separating software from hardware supports all three needs: fuller servers, automatic placement and quick recovery at another site.
Server Consolidation keeps existing servers busier and cuts costs, but it does not pick a server for each new workload.
Server Pooling picks the best server for new workloads, but it is not what restores mission systems after a catastrophe.
This plan restores systems after a catastrophe, but it does not keep the wing's existing servers busier day to day.

questions.stem: An airman must order a piece of hardware she will install and cable for a new virtual setup. Its processing power and memory will decide how many guests the setup can hold, and the whole setup will run on it. A copy of Windows will also be installed on it. Which component is she ordering?

answers.rationale: The hypervisor assigns memory to guests, but it is software, while she is ordering hardware to install and cable.
This system runs inside one guest, but the whole setup, every guest included, will run on what she orders.
The hardware on which every guest resides, whose processing power and memory limit the guests, may also carry its own Windows install.
This card is cabled hardware too, but its count does not decide how many guests the setup can hold.

questions.stem: One rack machine in an airman's unit now appears as eight machines, each running its own system and a single job such as handing out addresses. Other machines and client devices reach each of the eight exactly as they would a physical box, and users see nothing of the processors underneath. Which type is he using?

answers.rationale: Desktop Virtualization simulates workstations for users, but these eight are reached by other machines and clients like physical boxes.
Application Virtualization serves one program to many users rather than giving each of eight units its own system.
Storage Virtualization makes many storage devices appear as one, the reverse of one machine appearing as eight.
Partitioning one physical machine into smaller units that act toward clients like physical ones, hiding the processors, is this type.

questions.stem: After an untested change to one guest's settings, the unit's mission files stay on two guests running on separate hosts. Every record still matches its last approved copy, yet airmen with the right permissions now wait hours to open those files. Which concern did the change harm?

answers.rationale: Data that stays correct but cannot be opened promptly by those with appropriate authorization shows harm to this fundamental.
Integrity is about data staying uncompromised, and every record here still matches its approved copy.
This plan answers catastrophes far worse than one untested setting change on a single guest.
Load Balancing spreads work across the two running guests, yet authorized airmen still wait hours, so access itself was harmed.

questions.stem: An airman opens a set of data that every tree in her forest shares. When a new domain controller joins any domain of the forest, it receives its own replica of that data. Inside it, she finds entries that describe servers on the network. Which item is she looking at?

keywords.text: every tree in her forest shares

answers.rationale: The schema is shared by every tree, but it holds class and attribute definitions, not entries that describe actual servers.
Trees share one global catalog and it lists servers, but only global catalog servers hold it, not every new domain controller.
A new domain controller gets its own domain's data, but that data belongs to one domain, not to every tree in the forest.
Forest-wide data that every domain controller receives and that describes the servers on the network is this partition.

questions.stem: An airman opens a set of data that every tree in the forest shares. In it he sees that a user account carries fields such as an email address and a logon name. When he later adds a new user account, that data stays exactly the same. Which item is he looking at?

answers.rationale: Forest-wide data that lists the fields a user account carries, and stays the same when an account is added, is this template.
Configuration data is also shared by every tree, but it holds replication topology, not the fields a user account carries.
The domain partition holds user accounts and their fields, but only for one specific domain, not for every tree.
Trees share one global catalog, but it holds copies of actual objects, so a new user account changes it.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush shows an airman two entries in the base's directory. One stands for a single printer, and the other holds several user entries inside it. Both received a Globally Unique Identifier (GUID) when they were created. Which term covers both entries?

answers.rationale: A leaf could be the printer entry, but it cannot hold other entries, so it does not cover the second one.
Both the printer entry and the container entry are basic directory elements, each given its identifier when created.
Attributes describe an entry, such as its name, but they are not entries that receive their own identifier.
That container could be the second entry, but a single printer entry is not one.

questions.stem: An airman draws one area of the base network that covers two buildings whose networks share a fast, reliable link. That area serves users from several separate account databases, each with its own security policies. He draws several such areas inside the base's design. Which term names this area?

answers.rationale: A domain can cover two buildings, but it holds one account database, while this area serves several.
A forest can hold several account databases, but it is the outermost boundary of the design, not one of several areas.
An area set by well-linked networks that serves several domains and repeats within one design maps the physical network.
That subdivision groups users and computers inside one domain, not networks chosen for a fast link.

questions.stem: An airman adds a new machine to the base's domain so it has its own account there. Its disk holds only the squadron's database files, which other computers reach over the network. When users log on, a different machine checks who they are. Which kind of machine did he add?

answers.rationale: A machine in the domain that serves one dedicated database to others while another machine handles log-ons fits this role.
A domain controller would check who users are when they log on, but that job belongs to a different machine here.
A global catalog server holds directory entries from every domain in the forest, but this disk holds only database files.
A domain client has an account in the domain, but it runs a user's desktop instead of serving files to other computers.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush points to a machine that users on base need running before they can log on. It organizes all of the object data for its own network area in a hierarchical store. Its work covers only the accounts and computers of that one area. Which machine is he describing?

keywords.text: need running before they can log on

answers.rationale: A global catalog server is also needed for log-ons and stores its own domain's objects, but it also covers other domains.
A member server works inside one domain, but users do not need it running to log on.
A machine needed for log-ons that stores only its own domain's object data in a hierarchical store fits this role.
A domain client works inside one domain and its user logs on there, but it keeps no store of directory data.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush describes a unit that holds users and computers at the base and at a remote location reached over a slow link. Its own servers check every user's identity before that user reaches resources in it. Several of these units sit inside one tree that shares a common namespace. Which unit is he describing?

answers.rationale: A site has its own servers too, but separate sites are encouraged where a slow link divides a network.
A forest holds users and computers, but it is the top collection of trees, not a unit inside one.
That subdivision holds users and computers, but it has no servers of its own checking identities.
A unit spanning a slow link, with servers that authenticate its users and sitting inside a tree, is this logical unit.

questions.stem: An airman studies one grouping in the base's design. It contains several smaller groupings that each keep their own central account database. Those smaller groupings sit under two separate namespaces, and users, computers and groups anywhere inside its boundary can be reached. Which grouping is he studying?

answers.rationale: A grouping holding several account-database groupings under separate namespaces, with everything inside reachable, is the top collection of trees.
A domain tree holds domains that share one common namespace, not groupings under two separate namespaces.
A domain keeps one central account database itself; it does not contain several groupings that each keep their own.
That subdivision can contain smaller subdivisions, but those do not keep their own central account database.

questions.stem: An airman looks at the email address and phone number stored on a user account in the base's directory. Every user account carries the same set of these items. Yet two accounts hold different entries in them, which is how the two are told apart. Which term names these items?

answers.rationale: Object classes group objects of one type, but an email address and a phone number are pieces of information, not groupings.
Items every user account carries, holding different values that tell accounts apart, are the information each object holds.
The schema defines the same set for every user account, but it does not hold each account's own differing entries.
Each account is itself an object, and objects differ, but the same set of items on every account describes them.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush arranges the base's printers, users and computers, which sit in several buildings, into groups by the work they do together. His plan spans the base's two separate namespaces and reaches down to single objects such as one printer. Which part of the design is he working on?

answers.rationale: The physical structure also spans the whole base, but it covers how domains connect, not grouping by the work done.
Sites cover the buildings' networks by subnet, but they do not arrange single objects such as one printer into groups.
Grouping objects by how they work together, across namespaces and down to single objects, is this part of the design.
A domain tree groups objects too, but it shares one common namespace, so it cannot span two separate ones.

questions.stem: An airman examines the stored data on the one server in his building. One part holds the users and computers of his own domain. Another part of the same kind holds the class and attribute definitions for every object. Which term names each of these parts?

keywords.text: Another part of the same kind

answers.rationale: The schema is the part with class and attribute definitions, but it does not hold the users and computers of a domain.
Parts on one server, with domain users in one and definitions in another, are where this information is segregated and stored.
That subdivision holds users and computers, but it does not hold class and attribute definitions for every object.
A forest holds users and computers across many servers, so it is not a part stored on one server.

questions.stem: An airman's laptop reaches a base site for the first time, so its software sends the site's hostname to the local server and waits for the site's numeric address. Later, when the airman mistypes a hostname, the same software reports back an error message saying the host can't be found. Which choice names the kind of request the laptop sends?

answers.rationale: A request that ends in either the matching record or an error message when the host can't be found is exactly this kind.
In this type the resolver returns the best answer it can, but this software reports a definite error when the host can't be found.
This type needs the answer already stored on the device, but the laptop reaches this site for the first time.
This starts from a numeric address to find a hostname, but the laptop sent a hostname.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush sends a hostname from his workstation to the base's local server, which must search elsewhere to find its numeric address. In a capture he sees the local server stay in charge of the search, first contacting a root server, then a top-level server, and moving down until it reaches the machine that holds the address. Which choice names this process?

keywords.text: stay in charge of the search

answers.rationale: This type requires the resolver to return the record or an error, but the capture shows the local server walking down from the root.
In this type the answer is already known and returns at once, but this local server must search elsewhere.
A local server that stays in charge and works down from the root until it reaches the machine with the answer matches this type.
This starts from a numeric address to find a hostname, but the workstation sent a hostname.

questions.stem: An airman adds a machine at a remote site so the base's hostnames still resolve if the main machine fails. Edits to the base's host entries are made on the main machine and reach the new machine later. The new machine answers queries for the base's zones with authority. Which role does the new machine play?

answers.rationale: This role holds the master copy where edits are made, but here the edits are made on the main machine.
This role keeps only cached answers and is not authoritative for any zone, but the new machine answers with authority.
These machines form the upper-most layer of the whole tree, not a backup that one base adds at a remote site.
A backup machine that receives the main machine's changes later yet answers with authority for those zones fits this role.

questions.stem: An airman's laptop software asks a machine on base for the address of a host in the base's zone. Minutes after an airman changes that host's address on this same machine, its replies already carry the new address. The machine handles only the base's own zone. Which choice identifies the machine that replied?

answers.rationale: A machine on base that holds the zone's records, so a change there shows at once in its replies, answers with authority.
This server holds no zone to change and repeats cached answers until their time expires.
This is software on the laptop that asks, not the machine on base that replied.
These machines form the upper-most layer of the whole tree, not a machine handling only the base's zone.

questions.stem: An airman clicks a link to a base website, and his browser starts with only the site's complete hostname. Within moments the result of this one click arrives on his own computer, and the page opens. Which choice identifies the process that ran for this click?

answers.rationale: This starts from a numeric address to find a hostname, but his browser started with the hostname.
This copies zone information between servers, not a result that arrives on his own computer.
Turning a complete hostname into the numeric address a client needs, so the page can open, is this process.
This keeps copies on several servers matched over time, not a result produced for one click.

questions.stem: An airman studies a label that is written in many complete host addresses. The same label is shared by thousands of unrelated organizations, and it closes each of their addresses. The layer behind it is run by many more machines than the layer above it. Which layer does this label belong to?

answers.rationale: This layer is shared by everyone too, but it is assumed and usually not written in an address.
A written label shared by many organizations that ends their addresses, such as .mil, belongs to this layer.
This label is written too, but it names one organization and is followed by the ending.
This layer divides one organization by department, so thousands of unrelated organizations do not share it.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's organization already owns a registered name under .mil, and that name stays as it is. He wants the base's web hosts to carry one extra label of their own, used only by his organization, added to their addresses. Which layer would the extra label belong to?

keywords.text: one extra label of their own

answers.rationale: The registered name under .mil already sits at this layer and stays as it is, so the extra label goes one layer down.
This layer holds endings such as .mil shared by many organizations, not a label used only by one.
An extra label inside one organization, beneath its registered name, that groups some of its hosts belongs to this layer.
This upper-most layer is shared by everyone and is usually not written as a label.

questions.stem: An airman watches a component on her own laptop each time her browser or email client needs a host's numeric address. The component sends the question to the base's local server and relies on that server's reply. Which choice names this component?

answers.rationale: This answers questions from its own database, but this component relies on another server's reply.
This is stored data in a server database, but this component sends questions out.
Client code on the laptop that sends questions for programs and relies on a server's reply is this component.
This is a separate server that keeps cached answers, but this component runs on her own laptop.

questions.stem: An airman changes the address of the base's print server by editing just one piece of the database file on the base's server, and the rest of the file stays the same. Lookups for the print server then match that edited piece. Which choice names the piece he edited?

keywords.text: the rest of the file stays the same

answers.rationale: One stored entry in the database, edited alone and matched by lookups, is this component.
This is the part of the tree the whole file covers, not one piece edited while the rest stays the same.
This is a whole server that keeps cached answers, not a piece of data that lookups match.
This is client software on a host, not a piece of a database file on the server.

questions.stem: An airman maps the base's part of a worldwide system that turns hostnames into numeric addresses. She powers one of its machines down for maintenance. While it is down, the laptops' questions go to another of these machines, which answers in its place. Which choice identifies these machines?

answers.rationale: This client software sends the laptops' questions; it does not answer in another machine's place.
This is one stored entry, not a machine that can be powered down for maintenance.
This is a part of the tree that a machine serves, not a machine that receives questions.
Machines that receive questions from laptops and answer them, with one standing in for another, are this component.

questions.stem: This week an airman created a new area on the base's server, and he keeps adding to it. The area now holds many entries for the base's hosts along with a few sub-domains, and it covers only the base's own hosts. Which choice names that area?

answers.rationale: This is the whole tree, but this area covers only the base's own hosts.
An area created on a server to store the base's records and sub-domains is this.
This is one entry, but this area holds many entries and sub-domains.
This upper-most layer is shared worldwide and is not something an airman creates this week.

questions.stem: Each night the base's backup server sends a request to the main server. The reply carries every entry for the base's part of the naming tree in one batch, listed by hostname, and the backup server stores it so it can answer for the base the next day. Which choice names this process?

answers.rationale: This turns one hostname into an address for a client, not a nightly batch stored by a backup server.
This asks for one record or an error, not every entry of the base in one batch.
Moving a zone's entries from the main server to a backup server so it can answer for the zone is this process.
This starts from a numeric address to find a hostname, but this batch is listed by hostname.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush captures a lookup and sees each machine in the flow reply with an entry naming the next machine closer to the authoritative one. He then opens the base's zone file and finds the same entry type there, pointing to the machine that holds authority for the base's domain. Which entry type is he looking at?

keywords.text: the next machine closer to the authoritative one

answers.rationale: This type holds admin information for an authoritative machine, not an entry that names the next machine in a lookup.
This type creates an alias for a host and does not point to the machine that holds authority.
This type describes one host's details and is not passed between machines during a lookup.
An entry that names the next machine toward the authoritative one and points to the domain's authoritative machine is this type.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush explains that one consistent naming scheme covers every host on the Internet. In it, the web and mail hosts of one organization both sit under that organization's branch, and the whole arrangement runs from the uppermost layer down through every domain to the individual hosts. Which choice names this whole arrangement?

answers.rationale: A consistent scheme running from the uppermost layer through every domain to each host is this hierarchical tree.
This is one part a single server is responsible for, but this arrangement runs from the uppermost layer down.
This is only the uppermost layer, but this arrangement reaches down through every domain to the hosts.
This is one host's complete address, but this arrangement covers every host on the Internet.

questions.stem: An airman is building an address range on one of two servers on her network. Printers already hold fixed addresses inside that range. She types the printers' first and last address into one setup step so the server keeps those addresses for the printers alone. Which setup step is she completing?

answers.rationale: A client reservation makes the server always lease a device the same address, but these printers already hold fixed addresses.
Entering the start and end of a block the server must keep from clients, for devices with fixed addresses, is this step.
A delay sets how long one of two servers waits before offering, not which addresses are kept for the printers.
The starting and ending addresses of the scope set the whole range to lease out, not addresses kept for the printers.

questions.stem: Two servers on one network each lent the same address to a different laptop, and both laptops lost contact during the several days they held it. An airman finds she typed the same first and last address on both servers when she set them up. Which setting must she change on one server to end the conflict?

keywords.text: the same first and last address

answers.rationale: Lease duration only sets how long each laptop held its address; a shorter time would not stop both servers lending it.
A delay changes which server answers first, but both servers would still lend from the same first and last address.
Each server's block of lendable addresses must be unique, and these two were typed with the same first and last address.
Excluded addresses are never lent, so identical exclusions could not have made both servers lend the same address.

questions.stem: An airman's laptop got its network address from a server several days ago. As the agreed end date nears, the laptop checks back with that server to extend its hold so it can keep communicating on the network. Which term names the period during which the laptop may keep that address?

answers.rationale: The Request step is a single broadcast while an address is being obtained, not a period that has lasted several days.
A server lends a client its address for a set time, usually several days, and the client renews before it ends.
A scope is the range of addresses the laptop's address came from, and it has no end date to renew.
A delay is the server's wait before sending an offer, not the time a laptop keeps its address.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush captures the messages a laptop exchanges while it gets its network address. Two servers have each sent the laptop an address a moment earlier. The message he now examines goes out from the laptop to every machine on the network, and one server answers it right after. Which step is he examining?

keywords.text: to every machine on the network

answers.rationale: A laptop message to every machine, sent after two servers' addresses arrived and answered by one server, is this step.
Offer messages come from the servers, but this message goes out from the laptop.
Discover is also a laptop broadcast, but it comes before any server has sent an address.
Ack is the one server's reply, while this message went from the laptop to every machine.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush types some settings into an address server because devices on his network need them. When a laptop later joins, the server hands it those settings in the final step, as it acknowledges the laptop and records the lease in its database. Which term names those settings?

keywords.text: devices on his network need them

answers.rationale: Exclusions may serve fixed-address devices, but the server keeps those addresses back and never hands them to the laptop.
The subnet mask is set as part of the scope itself, while the acknowledgment step assigns the extra configured settings.
Settings added because clients need them and assigned as the server acknowledges the laptop are this term.
Lease duration is a required scope setting for how long addresses are loaned, not something added because devices need it.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's technicians already open their shared folders on a server, yet the server refuses when one of them tries to set its clock. He adds the needed ability to the technicians' group account itself, and from then on every member can set the clock. Which term names what he added?

answers.rationale: Permissions let the technicians open their folders, but setting the server clock is a task, not access to a file.
Abilities to perform predefined tasks, such as changing the date and time, are given to group accounts as this term.
These policy objects shape how systems behave for users, but the fix here was an ability added to the group account.
These lists sit on each folder to carry out its permissions, while this ability went on the group account.

questions.stem: An airman sets a folder on the shared drive so that one specific user can only read its files. He makes the change on the folder itself, and every new file later created inside it receives the same setting automatically. Which term names what he configured?

answers.rationale: Rights are given to a user or group to perform predefined tasks, but this change was made on the folder itself.
These policy objects define how a system behaves for a defined group of users, but this setting names one specific user.
This identifier names the user internally and is stored with the setting, but it does not decide that the user may only read.
Read-only access set on a folder, which new files inside inherit from their parent folder, is this term.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's section bought training software whose license allows it on one computer only. He installs it on one workstation and sets up logons that work on that machine alone, so the airmen in his section can use the software there. Which type of logon did he set up?

keywords.text: license allows it on one computer only

answers.rationale: A domain user account lets airmen use the software, but it is valid on any computer in the domain, not one machine.
The guest account is built in when Windows Server is installed and lacks a unique username, so it is not set up for each airman.
Logons that work on one machine alone keep a single-computer license from being violated, which fits this type.
An administrator account installs and manages software, but these logons are for the airmen to use the software.

questions.stem: An airman creates an item in the Microsoft Management Console (MMC) that tightens security options on desktops. He then associates the item with a domain, and every workstation in that domain takes on its settings. Which term names the item?

keywords.text: associates the item with a domain

answers.rationale: This guide also tightens security, but a defense agency generates it rather than the airman creating it in the console.
Items created in the console with security options and associated with a domain container are this term.
This list limits access, but it is attached to the one object it controls, not associated with a whole domain.
Rights can follow accounts across a domain, but they enable tasks rather than settings that workstations take on.

questions.stem: An airman tightens a new server's settings to close known weak spots, following a set of requirements he obtained for that server. Later a scanning tool flags two components as out of compliance with the set, and he records the findings on a checklist opened from it. Which term names the set?

answers.rationale: These policy objects tighten settings too, but compliance scans and findings checklists belong to vulnerability requirement sets.
Permissions help close access gaps, but a findings checklist is not opened from them.
These lists are built into each object to carry out permissions, not a set of requirements obtained for a server.
Requirements that correct vulnerabilities, checked by scanning tools and opened in a viewer to record findings, are this term.

questions.stem: An airman moves between offices and signs in at a different workstation each day with the same name and password. Her logon is kept in one central database on a controller, and an administrator decides there which network resources she can reach. Which type of logon does she have?

answers.rationale: A local user account keeps one name and password, but it logs on only to the computer where it was created.
The guest account lets people reach a computer's resources, but it has no unique username of its own.
An administrator controls other users' access, but this airman's own logon is the one being controlled.
A logon stored centrally on the controller, valid on any computer and controlled by admins, is this type.

questions.stem: When an airman joined her unit, an administrator created a logon that represents her alone and stores her name and Personal Identification Number (PIN) for sign-in. When she is later given read access to one folder, the logon's identity is written into that folder's access list. Which term names the logon?

answers.rationale: The guest account lets people log on without a unique username, so it cannot represent her alone.
This identifier is what gets written into the folder's list, but it does not store her sign-in details.
A logon that represents one person and stores her sign-in details, tracked in folder lists, is this term.
An administrator account has full rights to all resources, while this airman is given access one folder at a time.

questions.stem: An airman needs one quick overall picture of what is happening on his workstation. In the tool he opens, he clicks a tab that lists every service currently running, and another tab breaks down how each running program is performing. Which tool did he open?

answers.rationale: The Services Snap-in lists running services, but it has no tab that breaks down how each running program is performing.
Windows PowerShell can manage services, but it works through typed commands rather than tabs he clicks.
That console hosts administrative tools for maintaining networks and computers, not one quick overall picture of the workstation's activity.
A tool whose tabs give one bird's-eye view, including a tab of running services and one of program performance, fits here.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush asks an airman to check the background programs on a unit server. She opens a view devoted to those programs that shows each one currently running and its status. That view is one of the tools inside the administrative program that hosts her tools for maintaining networks, computers and other system components. Which tool is she using?

answers.rationale: A view of running services and their status, hosted with tools for maintaining networks, is the tool built upon the Microsoft Management Console (MMC).
The Services tab also lists running services, but it is a tab of Windows Task Manager, not a tool hosted with network maintenance tools.
That component manages services and their start settings behind the scenes, not a view she opens to read.
Windows Task Manager covers the whole system's activity in several tabs, while this view is devoted to services alone.

questions.stem: An airman presses Ctrl-Alt-Del and opens the program that gives her a bird's-eye view of her workstation. She clicks through to a view that lists every background helper currently running on Windows 10 and tells her which are running and which are stopped. Which view is she using?

answers.rationale: The Processes tab breaks down how running programs are performing, while this view lists background helpers and whether each is running.
The Services Snap-in is built upon the Microsoft Management Console (MMC), but she reached this view from Ctrl-Alt-Del.
Reached from Ctrl-Alt-Del, this view lists every current Windows 10 background helper and shows what is running and what is not.
Windows PowerShell manages services through typed commands, but she clicked through to a view in a program.

questions.stem: On an airman's base network, one central server holds information that every workstation in the domain contacts it for. Administrators push setting changes for the whole domain from that same place. When she signs on at any workstation, it matches what she types at sign-on to her user account. Which Windows component runs on that server?

answers.rationale: The Computer Browser Service keeps shared-resource information on one master computer, but it does not push domain-wide settings.
That service delivers software updates from servers to clients, but it holds no record that workstations contact or that matches sign-ons.
One central server that manages the whole domain and handles each user's identity at sign-on runs this Microsoft service.
That component controls access to each service on one machine, but this information sits on one server for the whole domain.

questions.stem: An airman types the classic Windows Commands his unit has always used line by line, and in the same window he also runs newer, more sophisticated scripts. His unit moved to this program from the first one Windows offered for routine automation. Which program is he using?

answers.rationale: The Command shell runs the classic Windows Commands, but it is the first program Windows offered, the one his unit moved away from.
Designed to extend the older shell, this program runs Windows Commands and cmdlets, a more extensible scripting language.
Windows Script Host runs sophisticated scripts inside the Command shell, but it is not a program he types commands into.
The command line tool sc.exe manages services; it does not run sophisticated scripts for routine automation.

questions.stem: An airman's unit has run its nightly backups for years from batch (.bat) files. She types each instruction herself, one line at a time, and for more sophisticated scripts she has to bring in a separate helper program that runs them inside this one. Which program fits?

answers.rationale: A program that runs batch-file backups typed line by line, and needs a separate host for more sophisticated scripts, matches every fact.
PowerShell brings its own more extensible scripting language with cmdlets, so it needs no separate helper for sophisticated scripts.
Windows Script Host is the separate helper that runs sophisticated scripts inside the program, not where she types each instruction.
The command line tool sc.exe takes typed instructions for services, but it does not run nightly backups from batch files.

questions.stem: An airman watches a group of helpers that run on a unit server at the same time. When he schedules a job, one of them picks it up, runs it and keeps checking on it until it is done. If one of them fails, the others take over its queued jobs and the server keeps running. Which kind of helper is this?

answers.rationale: Only one primary work process exists at a time, but this is a group of helpers running together.
Helpers that pick up jobs, execute them and monitor them until finished, sharing queued jobs when one fails, do the actual server work.
Communication processes hold the connections to agents and user interfaces rather than running and checking jobs.
The Client Server Runtime Process must never be ended, since ending it can crash the computer, yet these helpers cover for each other.

questions.stem: An airman double-clicks a mail program's icon, and its executable file starts running at once. It runs on his own desktop workstation. He then finds it by its file name on the Task Manager tab that breaks down how each running program is performing. Which term names what he is watching run?

answers.rationale: A server process is a task performed on a server and is typically started automatically, while this one started at his click.
Windows services run silently in the background and are shown on the Services tab, while he found this one on a different tab.
Communication processes are server processes that hold connections to agents and user interfaces, but this runs on his desktop workstation.
The action happening when an executable file runs after a click, listed by its file name in Task Manager, is this term.

questions.stem: Each night at 0200, the unit's main file host copies its shared folders to a backup drive while the office is empty. MSgt Rush can also kick off the same copy at any hour by typing one instruction. Once the copy finishes, that job ends until the next night. Which term names this job?

answers.rationale: Services run silently in the background to keep watching a subsystem, while this job ends once the copy finishes.
A cmdlet is a PowerShell command that could start the copy, but the nightly job itself runs on the file host at 0200.
A task performed on a server that usually starts automatically yet can also be started by a command is this term.
Communication processes hold connections to agents and user interfaces, while this job copies shared folders to a backup drive.

questions.stem: In a small office, each computer shares some of its own files, requests files from the others and holds equal authority. Which network model is the office using?

answers.rationale: Each computer sharing its own files, asking others for theirs and holding equal authority matches this decentralized model.
Client-server computers use a central computer as an intermediary instead of sharing resources directly with each other.
A domain is controlled from a single central point, so its computers do not hold equal authority.
The dedicated model is built around dedicated servers that manage resources for clients rather than equal computers.

questions.stem: A classmate describes one machine as middleware that adds services its Operating System (OS) lacks and links database machines and the end users. Which machine is it?

answers.rationale: A terminal server gives remote clients access to the network and its resources; it is not described as middleware.
A web server stores and transfers website data for browsers; it does not link database machines with end users.
That server stores resource information for administrators rather than serving as middleware.
Middleware that adds services for programs and links database machines with end users is this machine.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush shows a class a call center desk unit that leans on a central machine for nearly all of its processing. Which type is it?

answers.rationale: A thick client has many local applications and can run on its own without always being connected.
A unit that leans on a central machine for its work, as in call centers, is this client type.
A server does work for other systems; it is the central machine, not the unit leaning on it.

questions.stem: In a class, an airman reads about a service letting users log on remotely to a host computer and execute tasks there. Which service is it?

answers.rationale: That server moves files between computers; it does not let users execute tasks on a host.
A terminal server supplies applications and resources to remote clients rather than the remote log-on to execute tasks described here.
Remotely logging on to a host computer to execute tasks is what this protocol-based service allows.
A proxy server filters requests between clients and external servers instead of giving remote log-on.

questions.stem: An airman installs Windows Server 2022 inside each of three new virtual computers sharing one rack machine, so each gives users a standard computer experience. What is each Windows install called?

answers.rationale: The host server is the physical equipment the three virtual computers share, not the Windows install inside each.
The hypervisor manages communications between the host and the virtual computers; it is not installed inside them.
Each Windows install on virtual computer architecture gives users a standard computer experience, and one host can hold several.
Application Virtualization serves single programs from a central server, not a full Windows install in each computer.

questions.stem: An airman must sit at a rack server to set up its programs and settings, so he plugs in a keyboard, a mouse and a monitor. Which requirement covers these?

keywords.text: a keyboard, a mouse and a monitor

answers.rationale: This card carries the server's traffic to networks; a keyboard, mouse and monitor do not connect through it.
This memory sets how many guests the server supports; it is not how a person interacts with it.
This processor runs the server's work, but a person does not type or view settings through it.
A keyboard, mouse and monitor let a user interact with the server to set up its software and system.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's new host server lacks the on-board display chip most servers have, so he fits an add-in board into an open expansion slot. Which component does he add?

answers.rationale: This card can also sit in an expansion port, but it carries network traffic rather than driving a display.
Servers lacking integrated graphics need this component added as an adapter so a monitor can be connected.
This memory determines how many guests the server supports; it does not replace a missing display chip.
This processor runs the server's workloads; it is not the add-in that drives a monitor.

questions.stem: An airman's unit splits its programs from the physical equipment so several programs may use one machine as though each had complete control of it. What concept is this?

answers.rationale: Load Balancing divides a workload among machines on separate hardware; it is not the basic split itself.
Server Pooling lets software choose a host for each machine image; it builds on the split rather than being it.
Separating software from hardware so several programs use one machine, each acting as if in control, is the concept.
Patch Management keeps software fixed and current; it does not split programs from equipment.

questions.stem: From a laptop at home, an airman opens his full office workstation, which really runs on a remote server and is only simulated for him. Which type is this?

answers.rationale: Simulating a whole user workstation so it can be reached from a remotely connected device is what he uses.
Application Virtualization serves single programs from a central server, not the airman's full workstation.
Server Virtualization partitions a physical server into smaller virtual servers; it does not present a workstation.
Storage Virtualization pools storage devices into what looks like one device; it presents no workstation.

questions.stem: After the monthly patching of the guests' systems and applications, an airman must also patch the software link that handles traffic between the physical computer and its guests. Which component is that?

answers.rationale: The host server is the physical computer itself, not the software link between it and the guests.
A container is a logical partition for applications, not the software link between the computer and its guests.
The link that manages communications between the host and the virtual environment must be patched along with the systems.
This card moves network traffic in hardware; it is not the software link that manages the guests.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's server boots Windows Server 2022 from its drive, and he then installs VMware Workstation on it to create guests. Which term names Windows Server 2022 here?

answers.rationale: Windows Server 2022 is the primary software on the drive, the layer VMware Workstation runs on top of.
A Type 1 Hypervisor installs directly on hardware in place of Windows Server 2022, so nothing would run beneath it.
Each guest is created by VMware Workstation above Windows Server 2022, so it is not the software on the drive.
A container is a logical partition for applications that runs on the base software rather than being it.

questions.stem: An airman needs the Microsoft service that keeps one central listing of the base's servers, printers and user accounts so users find them quickly. Which service is it?

answers.rationale: A directory is any list of resources and their details, like a phone book, not a Microsoft network service.
A global catalog holds partial copies of entries from every domain, not the central service itself.
This Microsoft service provides a central listing of network resources and ways to find and access them quickly.
A domain controller is a server that holds and manages the database, not the service that provides the listing.

questions.stem: An airman learns that directory data is split into schema, configuration and domain parts. What is each part where that data is kept apart called?

keywords.text: split into schema, configuration and domain parts

answers.rationale: A forest is the collection of domain trees at the top of the structure, not a storage part.
That subdivision holds users, groups and computers; it is not one of the three storage parts.
An object is a single entry such as a user or printer, not a place where data is stored apart.
Schema, configuration and domain are the three places where directory data is segregated and logically stored.

questions.stem: On a design diagram, an airman must label the grouping that was created before every regional grouping and that the whole infrastructure is built on. Which label fits?

answers.rationale: A child domain is added later and branches out under the first one, so it is not the base.
A domain tree is a collection of domains sharing a namespace, not the single grouping created first.
This first grouping is created before any regional ones and is the foundation the rest of the infrastructure rests on.
That subdivision structure is created after the first grouping is deployed, so it cannot be the foundation.

questions.stem: An airman adds a shared printer to the base's directory, and it becomes one entry with its own name and location details. What is that single entry called?

answers.rationale: Attributes are the name and location details that describe the entry, not the entry itself.
That container holds many entries such as users and computers, not one printer's entry.
The schema holds class and attribute definitions for entries, not the printer's own entry.
A single entry standing for a network item such as a printer is this basic element.

questions.stem: An airman reads that one of these machines per site is recommended, and each holds a partial copy of every entry from the forest's other domains. Which machine is it?

keywords.text: one of these machines per site

answers.rationale: A domain controller holds objects unique to its own domain, not partial copies from the forest's other domains.
A member server handles a dedicated job such as file or print serving, not copies of directory entries.
This machine keeps partial copies of entries from all other domains, and one per site speeds up log-ons and searches.
A domain client is a computer with an account in the directory, not a holder of other domains' entries.

questions.stem: When an airman's admins create a new area on a server, they must choose whether it will hold forward or reverse lookups. What is that new area called?

answers.rationale: This is the whole hierarchy, which no single server creates as a new area.
This part of the hierarchy is created on a server and set for forward or reverse lookups.
This is one entry stored inside the new area, not the area itself.
This is the upper-most layer of servers shared by everyone, not an area admins create.

questions.stem: An airman types a printer's hostname, and the server returns its numeric address in a two-packet exchange. Which area of the server holds the records that answer her?

answers.rationale: This area answers the opposite request, returning a hostname for a numeric address.
Resolving a hostname to its numeric address is the most common task, and this area holds those records.
This is a copying process between servers, not an area that holds records.
This is the upper-most layer of the whole hierarchy, not an area on her server.

questions.stem: An airman troubleshooting a network sees only numeric addresses in a log. She wants the server to tell her which computer each address belongs to. Which area holds those records?

keywords.text: which computer each address belongs to

answers.rationale: This area answers the opposite request, returning an address for a hostname.
This is a copying process between servers, not an area that answers her request.
Starting from an address and getting back its hostname is what this area does, and it helps troubleshooting.
This is a layer of the hierarchy such as .mil, not an area that maps addresses to computers.

questions.stem: An airman's laptop sends one search to the local server, asking for the numeric address of a hostname. Besides lookup, what is this search called?

answers.rationale: This copies zone information between servers; it is not one search sent by a laptop.
This is the stored entry the search may find, not the search itself.
A search for a name-to-address or address-to-name answer is this, also called a lookup.
This is the server that receives the search, not the search itself.

questions.stem: Just under the very top of the naming tree sits a layer of many servers that answer for endings like .mil, .edu and .gov. What is this layer?

answers.rationale: This is the very top itself, the upper-most layer, not the layer under it.
This sits one layer lower, where most organization names stop.
This sits two layers lower and divides large organizations.
The layer under the very top that answers for endings like .mil and .edu is this.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush explains that, beneath endings like .mil, another band of servers answers for each organization's own area, such as the Air Force area under .mil. Which choice names this band?

answers.rationale: This adds a further division inside one organization, below each organization's own area.
Servers just beneath the endings that answer for each organization's own area form this layer.
This is the upper-most layer of the tree, above the endings themselves.
This is the layer of endings such as .mil, not the band beneath them.

questions.stem: An airman draws the whole naming hierarchy as one upside-down tree, from the top layer down to every host. What is that complete structure called?

answers.rationale: This is one part of the tree that a single server is responsible for, not the whole tree.
This is only the top layer of the tree, not the complete structure.
The whole hierarchical, upside-down tree is this, and it is divided into domains.
This is one layer just under the top, not the complete structure.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush sets up two address servers on one network, and he must keep their lendable address blocks from colliding. Which setting has to differ on each server?

answers.rationale: Exclusions are addresses a server keeps back, not the blocks each server lends to clients.
Each server's block of lendable addresses must be unique so that duplicate addresses are never leased.
A delay staggers which server answers first; it does not stop two servers lending the same addresses.
Lease duration sets how long an address is lent, not which addresses each server may lend.

questions.stem: On a network, which of these lets client machines obtain their addresses automatically from servers that lend them out for a set time?

answers.rationale: Name servers are among the settings a client is told about, but they do not lend the client its address.
The transmission protocol is part of the stack a client binds after leasing, so it does not lend addresses.
An internet address is what the client receives, but the addressing protocol itself does not lend addresses out.
This client-server protocol has servers lease addresses and other settings to the clients that request them.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush gives a newly formed group the most basic ability on its workstations, signing in, so its members can start work. What has he given the group?

answers.rationale: Permissions set access to particular files and folders, not the basic ability to sign in.
Signing in to a computer is one of the most basic of these, given to user or group accounts.
Group Policy shapes the working environment of accounts but is not the ability to sign in itself.
Credentials identify each member at sign-in, but they are not the ability the group was given.

questions.stem: On a Windows server, the read and write settings an airman sets on a folder are stored in a record joined to that folder. What is that record called?

answers.rationale: These policy objects define how a system behaves for a group of users rather than being joined to one folder.
These identifiers name a user internally and are stored in the record, but they are not the record itself.
Folder permissions are carried out through these, which are attached to the object they control.
These guides are configuration standards for a whole product, not a record joined to one folder.

questions.stem: When an airman types icf.rhope-ops.github.io, one Windows component on his workstation finds the matching Internet Protocol (IP) address and stores a local copy for reuse. Which component does this?

answers.rationale: This service resolves site addresses to numeric addresses and caches the results locally on the workstation.
The Computer Browser Service locates shared resources on neighboring computers, not the numeric address of a website.
That service oversees centralized domain management and identity functions, not finding a site's numeric address.
That service transfers files between machines over idle bandwidth, such as updates, not looking up site addresses.

questions.stem: An airman double-clicks the Yahoo icon, and Yahoo.exe starts running on his workstation. What is that running executable called?

answers.rationale: A server process is a task performed on a server, not a desktop application he opened himself.
The action happening when an executing file such as Yahoo.exe runs is exactly what this term names.
Communication processes hold connections to agents and user interfaces on a server, not a desktop application.
A cmdlet is a command run in PowerShell, not an executing file started by clicking an icon.

questions.stem: An airman learns that the specific operations a unit server runs are divided into two kinds. Which pair names those kinds?

answers.rationale: Agents and user interfaces are what one kind of server process connects, not the kinds themselves.
These are the two Windows command-line shells, not the kinds of server processes.
One kind does the actual server work and the other holds the connections to agents and user interfaces.
The primary work process and the remaining ones all belong to a single kind, so they cannot be both kinds.

questions.stem: In a base office, every computer takes one of two fixed roles, and desktops reach each other's data only through a central machine. Which network model is this?

answers.rationale: In peer-to-peer networks every computer talks directly with every other, with no central machine in between.
A workgroup has no centralized control, and its computers act as standalone systems.
Each computer set as one of two roles, with requests passing through a central machine, matches this dedicated model.
The non-dedicated model lets devices act as either role as needed, without a central go-between.

questions.stem: A supply catalog lists a desktop unit with its own drive and many local programs as a rich or fat type for office networks. Which type is it?

answers.rationale: A thin client relies heavily on a server and keeps little locally; it is not called rich or fat.
A workstation is a personal computer that may or may not join a network; those names belong elsewhere.
A server manages shared resources for others; it is not listed as a desktop type for users.
A desktop with its own drive and local programs, sold as rich or fat, is this client type.

questions.stem: In a small office, one machine acts as the file share and the print share for everyone simultaneously. Which kind of machine is it?

answers.rationale: A dedicated server provides specific services and nothing else, so it would not handle files and printing together.
One machine handling both file and print sharing at once is the flexible, non-dedicated role described here.
A single-purpose server is a file server only or a print server only, not both at once.
A virtual server converts one physical server into several separate machines for multiple users, not a file and print share.

questions.stem: In a large network, one machine is assigned a single backup service for everyone, and airmen reach it only over the network. Which kind of machine is it?

answers.rationale: A multipurpose server provides several services and local access for users, not one service alone.
A workstation is a personal computer an airman sits at for daily work, not one reached over the network.
A machine assigned one service for the network, with end users working elsewhere, fits this single-function role.
A virtual server converts one physical machine into several for multiple users, not one assigned service.

questions.stem: An airman splits one powerful rack computer into eight smaller virtual units, each acting toward clients just like a stand-alone machine. Which type is this?

answers.rationale: Partitioning one physical machine into smaller units that act like stand-alone machines is the most common type.
Desktop Virtualization simulates a user's workstation for a remote device; it does not split a rack computer.
Storage Virtualization joins many storage devices into what appears to be one, the reverse of splitting.
Application Virtualization serves one program to many users from a central computer rather than splitting it.

questions.stem: An airman is writing a briefing on software that partitions physical servers into smaller virtual servers and must name the product that currently leads the industry. Which should she name?

answers.rationale: Citrix XenServer appears among server virtualization software, but nothing calls it the industry leader.
Microsoft Hyper-V partitions servers too, yet the leader title belongs to another listed product.
Windows Server 2022 is a common host system in the Air Force, not the leading virtualization product.
This product is described as the current industry leader among server virtualization software.

questions.stem: An airman needs a product that partitions servers, comes from the maker of Windows Server, and installs directly on server hardware. Which should she choose?

answers.rationale: VMware Workstation is a hosted hypervisor that needs an installed system first, from another maker.
This product partitions servers, comes from the maker of Windows Server, and is a bare-metal hypervisor example.
Citrix XenServer partitions servers, but it does not come from the maker of Windows Server.
VMware Fusion is a hosted hypervisor example for Apple computers, not a bare-metal product from that maker.

questions.stem: An airman is building a new host server and wants its guests' traffic fast and redundant. Which component should he install four or more of?

answers.rationale: Four or more of these give the bandwidth, redundancy and speed guest traffic needs, or split traffic between networks.
This display processor lets a monitor connect to the host; adding four would not speed guest traffic.
This processor's power, along with memory, limits how many guests a host supports, not how traffic flows.
This memory decides how many guests the host can hold; it does not carry their traffic.

questions.stem: When requests spike, idle guests on a second physical machine are recruited so every guest carries part of the regular work. Which use of virtualization is this?

answers.rationale: Server Pooling picks a host for each new machine image; it does not recruit idle guests to share running work.
Server Consolidation puts many servers onto fewer hosts to cut costs, not spread a spike across guests.
This plan answers catastrophes like a lost data center, not a routine spike in requests.
Dividing the regular work among guests on separate hardware lets idle ones help, so resources are not left unused.

questions.stem: A unit installs one mapping program on a central server, and dozens of airmen use that single installed copy from their own devices at once. Which type is this?

answers.rationale: Server Virtualization partitions a physical server into smaller virtual servers rather than sharing one program.
One centrally installed program reached by many users at the same time is the defining use here.
Storage Virtualization pools storage devices into what appears to be one device; it does not serve programs.
User Profile Virtualization keeps a user's settings and data in a central share, not one installed program.

questions.stem: A large organization plans for catastrophes far worse than one crashed guest, such as losing a whole data center, by storing images of every guest. Which application is this?

answers.rationale: Load Balancing handles the loss of one machine by sharing work, not the loss of a whole data center.
Server Pooling picks hosts for machine images during normal work; it is not a plan for catastrophes.
Server Consolidation moves servers onto fewer hosts to save money, with no role in recovering from a catastrophe.
Plans for catastrophes like a lost data center rely on captured guest images that a hypervisor can start again.

questions.stem: An airman groups a parent network area and the two areas that branch out beneath it, because all three use one common namespace. What does the group form?

answers.rationale: A parent and the areas beneath it sharing one namespace make up this collection, with the root at its base.
A forest is a larger collection that holds one or more of these groups at the top of the structure.
A child domain is just one area branching out beneath the parent, not the whole group sharing the namespace.
A site is a range of subnets in the physical structure, not areas grouped by namespace.

questions.stem: An airman asks what sits at the very highest level of the base's directory design and marks the outer edge of where objects can be reached. Which element is it?

answers.rationale: A domain is a security boundary for its own users and resources, but it sits below the highest level.
This top-level collection of domain trees is the outermost boundary within which objects can be reached.
A domain tree is a group of domains sharing one namespace, which sits beneath the highest level.
The forest root domain is the first domain created, one part inside the top level rather than the whole.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush sketches the base's directory as a tree and circles a single printer entry where one branch stops. Which term names that printer entry?

answers.rationale: A single entry where a branch stops, holding no other entries, is an endpoint in the tree.
A child domain branches out from a root and holds further groupings, so the branch continues past it.
That container holds users, groups and computers, so a branch keeps going beyond it.
The forest root domain is the first domain created, at the base of the structure, not where a branch stops.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush defines one location in the physical design by listing the base's Internet Protocol (IP) subnets that belong together. What is he defining?

keywords.text: listing the base's Internet Protocol (IP) subnets

answers.rationale: A domain maps the logical structure of an organization, so a list of subnets does not define it.
A range of those subnets defines this part of the physical structure, which maps the network.
That subdivision splits a domain for users and computers; it is a logical grouping, not a subnet range.
A forest is the logical top collection of domain trees, not a location defined by subnets.

questions.stem: Before her laptop can open shared files on the base network, an airman must have her identity checked. Which server performs that check and enforces the security policy?

answers.rationale: A global catalog server helps locate resources in other domains, but it does not check identities or set policy.
A member server may hold the shared files, but it is not the server that checks identities.
A domain client is the laptop itself, a computer with an account that gets checked, not the checker.

Security scans search for malicious software, not a secret reused across sites.

questions.stem: Which Air Force program focuses on end-point security and on ports, protocols and services management?

This program limits what adversaries can collect as critical information about friendly actions, not end-point security.
This program protects classified information and unclassified information that needs controls, not end-point security.

questions.reviewCue: The program guarding each device at the edge of the network and the doorways it leaves open.
